questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Displacement of chloride, bromide and iodide ions by fluorine is generally not carried out in aqueous solution.
Reason (R): Fluorine is so reactive that it attacks water and displaces oxygen from it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true. Fluorine reacts with water as $2H_2O + 2F_2 \rightarrow 4HF + O_2$, so it displaces the oxygen of water.
A is true. Because $F_2$ reacts with the water itself, halide displacements using $F_2$ are not done in aqueous solution.
The reactivity of $F_2$ towards water is exactly why A holds, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation state of oxygen in the dioxygenyl cation, $O_2^+$, is:
questions.explanation:
For a polyatomic ion, the sum of the oxidation numbers equals the charge on the ion.
So $2x = +1$, which gives $x = +\frac{1}{2}$.
NCERT notes that in $O_2^+$ and $O_2^-$ the oxidation states are genuinely fractional: $+\frac{1}{2}$ and $-\frac{1}{2}$ respectively.
The value $-\frac{1}{2}$ belongs to superoxide, $O_2^-$.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: After zinc has reacted with copper nitrate solution, the colourless solution is tested for $Zn^{2+}$ ions. Which procedure and result confirm their presence?
options: Pass $H_2S$ and make the solution alkaline with ammonia; a white precipitate of ZnS forms
Pass $H_2S$ in acidic solution; a black precipitate of ZnS forms
Add starch solution; an intense blue colour appears
Add ammonia alone; a deep blue solution forms
questions.explanation:
According to NCERT, $Zn^{2+}$ is detected by passing $H_2S$ through the solution and then making it alkaline with ammonia.
This gives a white precipitate of zinc sulphide, ZnS.
Option (2) is wrong because ZnS is white, not black; black is the colour of CuS.
Starch gives a blue colour with iodine, not with $Zn^{2+}$, so option (3) is wrong.
A deep blue colour with ammonia is a test for $Cu^{2+}$, so option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
6.85 g of $Pb_3O_4$ is treated with excess nitric acid:
$Pb_3O_4 + 4HNO_3 \rightarrow 2Pb(NO_3)_2 + PbO_2 + 2H_2O$
What mass of $PbO_2$ remains unreacted? (Pb = 207, O = 16 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of $Pb_3O_4$ = 6.85 g; molar mass = 3(207) + 4(16) = 685 g/mol.
Moles of $Pb_3O_4$ = 6.85/685 = 0.01 mol.
Formula: $PbO_2$ is passive towards $HNO_3$, so 1 mol $Pb_3O_4$ gives 1 mol $PbO_2$. Molar mass of $PbO_2$ = 207 + 32 = 239 g/mol.
Substituting: mass = 0.01 × 239.
So mass of $PbO_2$ = 2.39 g.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Potassium dichromate oxidises sulphite ion in acidic solution: $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + SO_3^{2-} \rightarrow Cr^{3+} + SO_4^{2-}$. In the balanced net ionic equation with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of $H^+$?
questions.explanation:
Cr goes from +6 to +3, a decrease of 3 per Cr, or 6 per $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$. S goes from +4 to +6, an increase of 2, so 3 $SO_3^{2-}$ are needed.
Charge on the left is $-2 - 6 = -8$. Charge on the right is $+6 - 6 = 0$. Adding 8 $H^+$ to the left balances the charge.
Balancing H then needs 4 $H_2O$ on the right: $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3SO_3^{2-} + 8H^+ \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 3SO_4^{2-} + 4H_2O$.
14 is the coefficient of $H^+$ in the separate dichromate half-reaction, not in this overall equation.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When fluorine reacts with aqueous alkali, the products formed (apart from water) are:
options: $F^-$ and $FO^-$
$F^-$ and $OF_2$
$HF$ and $FO^-$ only
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives the reaction: $2F_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow 2F^- + OF_2 + H_2O$.
Fluorine is the most electronegative element and cannot show a positive oxidation state, so $FO^-$ or $FO_3^-$ cannot form.
In $OF_2$, it is oxygen that has the positive oxidation state (+2), while fluorine is $-1$.
So fluorine is only reduced and does not disproportionate, unlike $Cl_2$, $Br_2$ and $I_2$.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 4.6 g of sodium reacts completely with excess dioxygen to form $Na_2O$. How many moles of electrons are transferred from sodium to oxygen? (Atomic mass of Na = 23 g/mol)
options: 0.1 mol
0.2 mol
0.4 mol
0.05 mol
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of Na = 4.6 g, molar mass = 23 g/mol.
Formula: moles of Na = mass / molar mass. Each Na loses one electron: $Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-$.
Substituting: moles of Na = 4.6 / 23 = 0.2 mol, so moles of electrons = 0.2 × 1.
So electrons transferred = 0.2 mol. These are accepted by 0.05 mol $O_2$, which is why 0.05 mol is a trap.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the formation of sodium oxide, $4Na(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2Na_2O(s)$, how many electrons are gained by one $O_2$ molecule?
questions.explanation:
Sodium oxide is ionic, $(Na^+)_2O^{2-}$.
Each O atom gains 2 electrons to form $O^{2-}$, so one $O_2$ molecule gains 4 electrons: $O_2 + 4e^- \rightarrow 2O^{2-}$.
These 4 electrons come from 4 Na atoms: $4Na \rightarrow 4Na^+ + 4e^-$.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $2Cu_2O(s) + Cu_2S(s) \rightarrow 6Cu(s) + SO_2(g)$, which species acts as the reducing agent?
options: Cu(I) of $Cu_2O$
Sulphur of $Cu_2S$
Cu(I) of $Cu_2S$
Oxygen of $Cu_2O$
questions.explanation:
Oxidation numbers: Cu is +1 in both $Cu_2O$ and $Cu_2S$. S is −2 in $Cu_2S$ and +4 in $SO_2$. Cu is 0 in the metal.
Sulphur rises from −2 to +4. It is oxidised, so it is the reductant: it lowers the oxidation number of copper in both compounds.
Cu(I) falls from +1 to 0, so it is reduced and acts as the oxidant.
Oxygen stays at −2 throughout.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $2Na(s) + H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NaH(s)$, the product is ionic and can be written as $Na^+H^-$. Which description of hydrogen in this reaction is correct?
options: It is reduced and acts as an oxidising agent
It is oxidised and acts as a reducing agent
It is oxidised and acts as an oxidising agent
It is neither oxidised nor reduced
questions.explanation:
In $Na^+H^-$, each H atom has become a hydride ion, $H^-$.
The reduction half is $H_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2H^-$, so hydrogen gains electrons and is reduced.
A species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.
Sodium donates the electrons, so sodium is the reducing agent.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + 6I^- + 4H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + 3I_2 + 8OH^-}$, how many electrons are gained by one permanganate ion?
questions.explanation:
Mn has oxidation number +7 in $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ and +4 in $\mathrm{MnO_2}$.
The change is 7 – 4 = 3, so each permanganate ion gains 3 electrons. Its n-factor here is 3.
In total, 2 $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ gain 6 electrons, matching the 6 electrons lost by 6 $\mathrm{I^-}$.
The value 5 applies only in acidic medium, where $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ goes to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$. The value 6 is the total for the whole equation, not per ion.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Standard reduction potentials (in V) are given: $I_2/I^-$ = +0.54, $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}$ = +0.77, $Br_2/Br^-$ = +1.09, $Cl_2/Cl^-$ = +1.36, $Ni^{2+}/Ni$ = –0.25, $Pb^{2+}/Pb$ = –0.13, $Zn^{2+}/Zn$ = –0.76.
How many of the following species can oxidise $I^-$ to $I_2$ under standard conditions?
$Fe^{3+}$, $Br_2$, $Ni^{2+}$, $Cl_2$, $Pb^{2+}$, $Zn^{2+}$
questions.explanation:
A species can oxidise $I^-$ only if its reduction potential is higher than that of $I_2/I^-$ (+0.54 V).
$Fe^{3+}$ (0.77), $Br_2$ (1.09) and $Cl_2$ (1.36) are all above 0.54 V, so they can oxidise $I^-$.
$Ni^{2+}$ (–0.25), $Pb^{2+}$ (–0.13) and $Zn^{2+}$ (–0.76) are far below 0.54 V, so they cannot.
Count = 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In oxygen difluoride ($OF_2$), oxygen has an oxidation number of +2.
Statement II: In potassium superoxide ($KO_2$), each oxygen atom has an oxidation number of –1.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Fluorine is always –1, so in $OF_2$: x + 2(–1) = 0, which gives x = +2.
Statement II is incorrect. In $KO_2$, K is +1, so 2x = –1 and each O is $-\frac{1}{2}$.
An oxygen value of –1 belongs to peroxides such as $Na_2O_2$, not superoxides.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When $Pb_3O_4$ is treated with nitric acid, $PbO_2$ is left behind as a solid product.
Reason (R): $HNO_3$ is itself an oxidising agent, so it does not react with the oxidant $PbO_2$; only the basic oxide PbO undergoes an acid–base reaction with it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The reaction is $Pb_3O_4 + 4HNO_3 \rightarrow 2Pb(NO_3)_2 + PbO_2 + 2H_2O$.
R is true. Basic PbO reacts with the acid: $2PbO + 4HNO_3 \rightarrow 2Pb(NO_3)_2 + 2H_2O$.
Since both $HNO_3$ and $PbO_2$ are oxidants, $PbO_2$ stays passive and remains unreacted.
R therefore correctly explains A. With HCl, by contrast, $PbO_2$ oxidises $Cl^-$ to $Cl_2$.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: In $KI_3$, iodine has an average oxidation number of $-\frac{1}{3}$, but in reality two iodine atoms are at 0 and one is at –1
In $H_2S_4O_6$, the two central sulphur atoms have oxidation number 0 while the two terminal ones are +5
In $Mn_3O_4$, two manganese atoms are in the +2 state and one is in the +3 state
In $Br_3O_8$, the sum of the real oxidation numbers of the three bromine atoms is +16
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $I_3^-$ is $I_2 + I^-$, giving states 0, 0 and −1, with average −1/3.
(2) Correct: $S_4O_6^{2-}$ has states +5, 0, 0, +5 (average 2.5).
(3) Incorrect: $Mn_3O_4$ = MnO·$Mn_2O_3$, so one Mn is +2 and two are +3. Check: $\frac{2+3+3}{3} = \frac{8}{3}$. The stated arrangement would give 7/3.
(4) Correct: 6 + 4 + 6 = 16, which matches 3 × 16/3.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In how many of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation number of −1?
LiH, HCl, NaH, $H_2O$, $CaH_2$, $CH_4$, KH
questions.explanation:
Rule: hydrogen has oxidation number +1, except in binary compounds with metals, where it is −1.
LiH, NaH, $CaH_2$ and KH are binary metal hydrides, so H is −1 in each. That makes 4 compounds.
In HCl, $H_2O$ and $CH_4$, H is bonded to non-metals, so it is +1.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Zinc reduces $Cu^{2+}$ ions in solution, and copper reduces $Ag^{+}$ ions in solution. What is the correct order of the tendency of these metals to release electrons?
options: Ag > Cu > Zn
Zn > Cu > Ag
Cu > Zn > Ag
Zn > Ag > Cu
questions.explanation:
Zinc gives electrons to $Cu^{2+}$, so Zn releases electrons more readily than Cu.
Copper gives electrons to $Ag^{+}$, so Cu releases electrons more readily than Ag.
Combining the two results gives Zn > Cu > Ag.
This comparison is the starting point for building a metal activity (electrochemical) series.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In the reaction $2Na(s) + H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NaH(s)$, hydrogen is reduced and sodium is oxidised.
Statement II: The simple rules "addition of hydrogen is reduction" and "removal of hydrogen is oxidation" cannot directly decide this case; it needs a careful application of electronegativity.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Hydrogen is more electronegative than sodium. Adding the electropositive Na to hydrogen means hydrogen is reduced, and Na is oxidised.
Statement II is correct. Hydrogen is a reactant element here, so the hydrogen-based rules give no direct verdict. NCERT notes that only careful use of electronegativity lets us infer the result.
This case motivated the electron-transfer definition.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following reactions have their reducing agent correctly identified?
(i) $CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O$ ; reducing agent: $H_2$
(ii) $Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2$ ; reducing agent: $CO$
(iii) $2AgBr + C_6H_6O_2 \rightarrow 2Ag + 2HBr + C_6H_4O_2$ ; reducing agent: $AgBr$
(iv) $N_2H_4 + 2H_2O_2 \rightarrow N_2 + 4H_2O$ ; reducing agent: $H_2O_2$
(v) $Pb + PbO_2 + 2H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2PbSO_4 + 2H_2O$ ; reducing agent: $Pb$
questions.explanation:
The reducing agent is the species whose element's oxidation number increases.
(i) Correct: H goes from 0 to $+1$, so $H_2$ is the reductant.
(ii) Correct: C goes from $+2$ to $+4$, so $CO$ is the reductant.
(iii) Wrong: Ag goes from $+1$ to 0, so $AgBr$ is the oxidant. Hydroquinone ($C_6H_6O_2$) is the reductant.
(iv) Wrong: O goes from $-1$ to $-2$, so $H_2O_2$ is the oxidant. N goes from $-2$ to 0, so $N_2H_4$ is the reductant.
(v) Correct: Pb goes from 0 to $+2$, so Pb is the reductant.
Three reactions are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Why can $F_2$ be obtained from fluoride ions only by electrolytic oxidation and not by any chemical oxidising agent?
options: $F^-$ ion is too large to be oxidised chemically
$F_2$ is the strongest oxidising agent, so no chemical oxidant can oxidise $F^-$
Fluorides are insoluble in water
Fluorine shows a positive oxidation state in most of its compounds
questions.explanation:
To obtain $F_2$ from $F^-$, the reaction $2F^- \rightarrow F_2 + 2e^-$ must occur.
A chemical oxidant would have to be stronger than $F_2$. But fluorine is the strongest oxidising agent ($E^\circ$ = +2.87 V), so no such reagent exists.
Hence electrolysis is the only route.
$F^-$ is actually small, many fluorides are soluble, and fluorine never shows a positive oxidation state, so the other options are wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In $H_2SO_5$, applying the rules with every oxygen taken as –2 gives sulphur an oxidation number of +8.
Statement II: The actual oxidation number of sulphur in $H_2SO_5$ is +6, because two of its oxygen atoms form a peroxide (–O–O–) linkage and are each assigned –1.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. $2(+1) + x + 5(-2) = 0$ gives $x = +8$.
This value is impossible, since the highest oxidation number of sulphur (group 16) is +6. That is the fallacy.
Statement II is correct. Because of the peroxo linkage, $2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0$, which gives $x = +6$.
So only the structure reveals the true oxidation state.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The word "redox" was coined for a class of chemical reactions because:
options: such reactions always involve dioxygen
oxidation and reduction always occur simultaneously in them
such reactions always produce an oxide and a hydride
only metals take part in such reactions
questions.explanation:
NCERT re-examined reactions such as HgCl2 + SnCl2. It found that whenever one species is oxidised, another is reduced at the same time.
This simultaneous pairing gave the combined name red-ox.
Many redox reactions involve no O2 at all, for example Mg + Cl2, so option (1) fails.
They need not involve metals or form oxides and hydrides.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous solution containing both KBr and KI is shaken with a little $CCl_4$. Chlorine water is then added drop by drop with shaking. Use $E^\circ(Br_2/Br^-) = 1.09$ V, $E^\circ(I_2/I^-) = 0.54$ V and $E^\circ(Cl_2/Cl^-) = 1.36$ V. Which observation is made first in the $CCl_4$ layer, and why?
options: Orange-brown colour, because $Br^-$ is a stronger reducing agent than $I^-$
Violet colour, because $I^-$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Br^-$ and is oxidised first
Violet colour, because $Cl_2$ cannot oxidise $Br^-$ at all
No colour, because $Cl_2$ oxidises $K^+$ ions preferentially
questions.explanation:
A lower $E^\circ$ of a couple means its reduced form is a stronger reducing agent. Since 0.54 V < 1.09 V, $I^-$ is a stronger reductant than $Br^-$.
So the added $Cl_2$ first oxidises $I^-$: $Cl_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + I_2$. The $I_2$ turns the $CCl_4$ layer violet.
$Cl_2$ can also oxidise $Br^-$ (1.36 V > 1.09 V), so option (3) is wrong. This happens only after most of the $I^-$ has been used up.
$K^+$ cannot be oxidised further, so option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: $Hg_2Cl_2$, written in Stock notation as $Hg_2(I)Cl_2$, is the reduced form of $Hg(II)Cl_2$
The highest oxidation number shown by chlorine in its compounds is +7
In carbon suboxide, $C_3O_2$, the two terminal carbon atoms are in the +2 state and the central carbon is in the zero state
In $Fe_3O_4$, every iron atom is present in the $+\frac{8}{3}$ oxidation state
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Hg goes from +2 to +1, i.e. a lower oxidation number, so $Hg_2Cl_2$ is the reduced form.
(2) Correct: chlorine is in group 17, so its highest oxidation number is 17 − 10 = +7, as in $HClO_4$.
(3) Correct: the structure O=C=C=C=O gives +2, 0, +2, which averages to 4/3.
(4) Incorrect: $+\frac{8}{3}$ is only an average. $Fe_3O_4$ is a mixed oxide containing Fe(II) and Fe(III).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In how many of the following reactions is the species written in brackets the reducing agent?
(i) $CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O$  [$H_2$]
(ii) $Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2$  [$CO$]
(iii) $4NH_3 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 4NO + 6H_2O$  [$O_2$]
(iv) $N_2H_4 + 2H_2O_2 \rightarrow N_2 + 4H_2O$  [$N_2H_4$]
(v) $Pb + PbO_2 + 2H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2PbSO_4 + 2H_2O$  [$PbO_2$]
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: H goes from 0 to +1, so $H_2$ is the reductant.
(ii) Correct: C goes from +2 to +4, so CO is the reductant.
(iii) Wrong: O goes from 0 to −2, so $O_2$ is the oxidant. $NH_3$ (N: −3 to +2) is the reductant.
(iv) Correct: N goes from −2 to 0, so $N_2H_4$ is the reductant.
(v) Wrong: Pb in $PbO_2$ goes from +4 to +2, so $PbO_2$ is the oxidant. Pb metal is the reductant.
Three reactions qualify.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
A galvanic cell uses the reaction $2Al(s) + 3Cu^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow 2Al^{3+}(aq) + 3Cu(s)$ under standard conditions.
Given $E^\circ(Al^{3+}/Al) = -1.66$ V and $E^\circ(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = +0.34$ V, what is the standard emf of the cell?
(Use $E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode}$.)
questions.explanation:
Given: Al is oxidised, so it is the anode ($-1.66$ V). Cu²⁺ is reduced, so Cu is the cathode ($+0.34$ V).
Formula: $E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode}$.
Substituting: $E^\circ_{cell} = 0.34 - (-1.66)$.
So $E^\circ_{cell} = 2.00$ V.
The stoichiometric coefficients do not multiply $E^\circ$, and 1.32 V comes from simply adding the two values.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The perchlorate ion, $ClO_4^-$, does not undergo disproportionation.
Reason (R): In $ClO_4^-$, chlorine is in its highest oxidation state, +7, so it cannot be oxidised further.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
In disproportionation, an element in an intermediate oxidation state is oxidised and reduced at the same time.
In $ClO_4^-$: x + 4(–2) = –1, so x = +7. This is the highest oxidation state of chlorine (group 17).
Chlorine at +7 cannot be oxidised further, so it cannot disproportionate. A is true.
R is true and it is the reason for A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following species contain the indicated element in the $+6$ oxidation state?
Mn in $K_2MnO_4$; S in $H_2S_2O_7$; Cr in $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$; S in $SO_3^{2-}$; Xe in $XeO_3$; Mn in $MnO_4^-$
questions.explanation:
$K_2MnO_4$: 2(+1) + x + 4(−2) = 0, so Mn = +6. Counted.
$H_2S_2O_7$: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0, so S = +6. Counted.
$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$: 2x − 14 = −2, so Cr = +6. Counted.
$SO_3^{2-}$: x − 6 = −2, so S = +4. Not counted.
$XeO_3$: x − 6 = 0, so Xe = +6. Counted.
$MnO_4^-$: x − 8 = −1, so Mn = +7. Not counted.
Four species have the +6 state.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen peroxide oxidises $Fe^{2+}$ to $Fe^{3+}$ in acidic solution, and water is formed. Which statement about the balanced equation is correct?
options: $H_2O_2$ acts as the reducing agent
Two moles of $Fe^{2+}$ are oxidised per mole of $H_2O_2$
$H^+$ ions appear on the product side
Oxygen changes its oxidation number from −1 to 0
questions.explanation:
The balanced equation is $H_2O_2 + 2Fe^{2+} + 2H^+ \rightarrow 2Fe^{3+} + 2H_2O$.
(1) Incorrect: $H_2O_2$ accepts electrons, so it is the oxidant.
(2) Correct: each O gains 1 electron (−1 to −2), so 2 electrons are needed per $H_2O_2$, supplied by 2 $Fe^{2+}$.
(3) Incorrect: $H^+$ is consumed and appears on the reactant side.
(4) Incorrect: O goes from −1 to −2, not to 0.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Separate samples containing equal numbers of moles of $Cl_2$, $O_2$ and S are each completely converted by sodium into NaCl, $Na_2O$ and $Na_2S$ respectively. What is the ratio of moles of sodium consumed in the three cases?
questions.explanation:
Each Na atom donates exactly one electron, so moles of Na equal moles of electrons accepted.
$Cl_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-$: 2 electrons per $Cl_2$.
$O_2 + 4e^- \rightarrow 2O^{2-}$: 4 electrons per $O_2$.
$S + 2e^- \rightarrow S^{2-}$: 2 electrons per S.
Per mole of oxidant, Na needed = 2 : 4 : 2 = 1 : 2 : 1.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Red lead, $Pb_3O_4$, is best described as a stoichiometric mixture of:
options: 1 mol PbO and 2 mol $PbO_2$
3 mol PbO and 1 mol O
2 mol PbO and 1 mol $PbO_2$
1 mol $Pb_2O_3$ and 1 mol PbO
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes $Pb_3O_4$ as 2PbO + $PbO_2$.
Check: this gives 3 Pb and 4 O. ✓
So two Pb atoms are in the +2 state and one is in the +4 state. This explains the average value of $\frac{8}{3}$.
Option (1) gives $Pb_3O_5$, so the formula does not match.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $AgF_2$, if formed, behaves as a very strong oxidising agent.
Reason (R): Silver is in the uncommon +2 state in $AgF_2$ and readily accepts an electron to attain its stable +1 state.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
F is always −1, so Ag in $AgF_2$ is +2.
The stable oxidation state of silver is +1, so Ag(II) is unstable and tends to gain an electron: $Ag^{2+} + e^- \rightarrow Ag^+$.
This strong tendency to accept electrons makes $AgF_2$ a powerful oxidant.
So A is true, R is true, and R explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Caesium superoxide has the formula $CsO_2$. What is the oxidation number of each oxygen atom in it?
questions.explanation:
Cs is an alkali metal, so its oxidation number is +1.
The compound is neutral: $+1 + 2x = 0$, so $x = -\frac{1}{2}$.
In superoxides the oxygen atoms are linked to each other, and NCERT assigns each O an oxidation number of $-\frac{1}{2}$.
The value $-1$ applies to peroxides such as $Na_2O_2$, not to superoxides.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction).
List-I:
(A) $Cr_2O_3 + 2Al \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 2Cr$
(B) $2H_2O + 2F_2 \rightarrow 4HF + O_2$
(C) $3Mg + N_2 \rightarrow Mg_3N_2$
(D) $2NaH \rightarrow 2Na + H_2$
List-II:
(I) Combination
(II) Decomposition
(III) Metal displacement
(IV) Non-metal displacement
options: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
questions.explanation:
(A) Al displaces Cr from its oxide, so this is metal displacement (III).
(B) Fluorine displaces the oxygen of water, so this is non-metal displacement (IV).
(C) Two elements combine to form one compound, so this is combination (I).
(D) A compound breaks into its elements, so this is decomposition (II).
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: When white phosphorus ($P_4$) reacts with alkali, it gives $PH_3$ and $H_2PO_2^-$, in which phosphorus has oxidation numbers $-3$ and $+1$ respectively.
Statement II: When $S_8$ reacts with alkali, it gives $S^{2-}$ and $S_2O_3^{2-}$, in which sulphur has oxidation numbers $-2$ and $+2$ respectively.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In $PH_3$: P + 3(+1) = 0, so P = $-3$. In $H_2PO_2^-$: 2(+1) + P + 2($-2$) = $-1$, so P = +1. Phosphorus starts at 0 in $P_4$ and goes both down and up.
Statement II is correct. In $S^{2-}$, S = $-2$. In $S_2O_3^{2-}$: 2S + 3($-2$) = $-2$, so S = +2 (average). Sulphur starts at 0 in $S_8$.
Both are disproportionation reactions in alkaline medium.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the reaction $2FeCl_3(aq) + H_2(g) \rightarrow 2FeCl_2(aq) + 2HCl(aq)$, ferric chloride is reduced.
Reason (R): Ferric chloride is reduced because hydrogen gets added to it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. FeCl3 becomes FeCl2, so chlorine, an electronegative element, is removed from it. That is reduction.
R is false. Hydrogen is not added to the iron chloride. Hydrogen combines with the removed chlorine to form HCl.
The correct basis is removal of an electronegative element, not addition of hydrogen.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I (conversion) with List-II (number of electrons gained or lost as written):
List-I
(A) $MnO_4^- \rightarrow MnO_2$ (basic medium)
(B) $MnO_4^- \rightarrow Mn^{2+}$ (acidic medium)
(C) $Cr_2O_7^{2-} \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+}$
(D) $2I^- \rightarrow I_2$
List-II
(i) 2
(ii) 3
(iii) 5
(iv) 6
options: A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(i)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(iv), D-(i)
A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(ii), D-(i)
questions.explanation:
(A) Mn goes from +7 to +4, so 3 electrons are gained: (ii).
(B) Mn goes from +7 to +2, so 5 electrons are gained: (iii).
(C) Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, and there are two Cr atoms, so 6 electrons are gained: (iv).
(D) Each I goes from −1 to 0, and there are two I atoms, so 2 electrons are lost: (i).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Using the standard electrode potentials
$Cl_2/Cl^- = 1.36$ V, $Br_2/Br^- = 1.09$ V, $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+} = 0.77$ V, $I_2/I^- = 0.54$ V, $Cu^{2+}/Cu = 0.34$ V, $Fe^{2+}/Fe = -0.44$ V, $Zn^{2+}/Zn = -0.76$ V,
identify the reaction that is NOT feasible under standard conditions.
options: $Cl_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + Br_2$
$Fe + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{2+} + Cu$
$I_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2I^- + Br_2$
$2Fe^{3+} + Zn \rightarrow 2Fe^{2+} + Zn^{2+}$
questions.explanation:
A reaction is feasible when the oxidant's couple has a higher $E^\circ$ than the reductant's couple.
(1) Cl₂ (1.36 V) oxidises Br⁻ (1.09 V): feasible.
(2) Cu²⁺ (0.34 V) oxidises Fe (−0.44 V): feasible.
(3) I₂ (0.54 V) would have to oxidise Br⁻ (1.09 V). I₂ is the weaker oxidant, so this is not feasible.
(4) Fe³⁺ (0.77 V) oxidises Zn (−0.76 V): feasible.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (experiment) with List-II (observation or conclusion).
List-I:
(P) Zn strip in $Cu(NO_3)_2$ solution
(Q) Cu strip in $ZnSO_4$ solution
(R) Cu wire in $AgNO_3$ solution
(S) Co metal in $NiSO_4$ solution
List-II:
(i) Solution turns blue
(ii) Blue colour of the solution disappears
(iii) Neither reactants nor products greatly favoured
(iv) No detectable reaction
options: P-ii, Q-iv, R-i, S-iii
P-i, Q-iv, R-ii, S-iii
P-ii, Q-iii, R-i, S-iv
P-iv, Q-ii, R-iii, S-i
questions.explanation:
P: $Cu^{2+}$ is reduced and removed from solution, so the blue colour disappears (ii).
Q: Cu cannot reduce $Zn^{2+}$; not even the sensitive CuS test detects any $Cu^{2+}$ (iv).
R: Cu is oxidised to $Cu^{2+}$, so the solution turns blue (i).
S: $Co^{2+}$ and $Ni^{2+}$ are both present at moderate concentrations, so neither side is greatly favoured (iii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (oxidation number of each oxygen atom):
List-I: (A) $Na_2O_2$ (B) $KO_2$ (C) $OF_2$ (D) $O_2F_2$
List-II: (i) +2 (ii) –1 (iii) +1 (iv) $-\frac{1}{2}$
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i)
questions.explanation:
(A) $Na_2O_2$ is a peroxide: 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so x = –1.
(B) $KO_2$ is a superoxide: +1 + 2x = 0, so x = $-\frac{1}{2}$.
(C) $OF_2$: fluorine is always –1, so x = +2.
(D) $O_2F_2$: 2x + 2(–1) = 0, so x = +1.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in oxygen difluoride, $OF_2$?
questions.explanation:
Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so it is always $-1$ in its compounds.
In $OF_2$, let the O.N. of oxygen be x. Then x + 2(−1) = 0, so x = +2.
This is one of the rare exceptions where oxygen has a positive oxidation number.
$+1$ is the value for oxygen in $O_2F_2$, not $OF_2$.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine belongs to group 17 of the long form of the periodic table. What is the highest oxidation number chlorine can show, as in $HClO_4$?
questions.explanation:
For groups other than 1 and 2, the highest oxidation number of a representative element is (group number − 10).
For chlorine this is $17 - 10 = +7$.
Check with $HClO_4$: $+1 + x + 4(-2) = 0$, so $x = +7$.
+17 wrongly uses the group number directly. +5 (as in chlorate) and +1 (as in HClO) are lower states, not the highest.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The reaction $(CN)_2(g) + 2OH^-(aq) \rightarrow CN^-(aq) + CNO^-(aq) + H_2O(l)$ is a disproportionation reaction.
Reason (R): Carbon in cyanogen is in the +3 oxidation state, which lies between its oxidation states of +2 in $CN^-$ and +4 in $CNO^-$.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Take N = $-3$ throughout.
In $(CN)_2$: C + ($-3$) = 0 per CN unit, so C = +3.
In $CN^-$: C + ($-3$) = $-1$, so C = +2. Carbon is reduced.
In $CNO^-$: C + ($-3$) + ($-2$) = $-1$, so C = +4. Carbon is oxidised.
The same element in an intermediate state is both oxidised and reduced, so A is true.
R states exactly this, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the compound names in List-I with their formulas in List-II.
List-I:
(A) Aurous chloride
(B) Stannic chloride
(C) Mercurous chloride
(D) Iron(III) sulphate
List-II:
(p) $Hg_2Cl_2$
(q) $AuCl$
(r) $Fe_2(SO_4)_3$
(s) $SnCl_4$
options: A-q, B-s, C-p, D-r
A-q, B-p, C-s, D-r
A-s, B-q, C-p, D-r
A-q, B-s, C-r, D-p
questions.explanation:
A: Aurous means Au(I), so the formula is AuCl (q).
B: Stannic means Sn(IV), so the formula is $SnCl_4$ (s).
C: Mercurous means Hg(I). It exists as the dimer $Hg_2Cl_2$, written Hg$_2$(I)Cl$_2$ in Stock notation (p).
D: For iron(III) sulphate, two $Fe^{3+}$ ions balance three $SO_4^{2-}$ ions, giving $Fe_2(SO_4)_3$ (r).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In basic medium, dichlorine heptoxide is reduced by hydrogen peroxide according to the skeletal equation $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7 + H_2O_2 \rightarrow ClO_2^- + O_2}$. What mass of $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ is needed to completely reduce 0.10 mol of $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$? (Atomic masses: H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation:
Given: each Cl changes from +7 to +3, so 1 $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$ gains 2 × 4 = 8 electrons. Each $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ loses 2 electrons (O changes from –1 to 0).
Formula: the electron balance gives 1 $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$ : 4 $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$. The balanced equation is $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7 + 4H_2O_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow 2ClO_2^- + 4O_2 + 5H_2O}$.
Substituting: $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ needed = 4 × 0.10 = 0.40 mol; mass = 0.40 × 34 = 13.6 g.
The option 3.4 g wrongly assumes a 1 : 1 ratio.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In titrations with $KMnO_4$, the first lasting pink tinge marks the end point, so no external indicator is required.
Statement II: Like $KMnO_4$, $K_2Cr_2O_7$ acts as a self-indicator, and its end point is seen as an intense blue colour of its own.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. $MnO_4^-$ is intensely coloured, so a faint pink colour persists once the reductant (such as $Fe^{2+}$ or $C_2O_4^{2-}$) is used up.
Statement II is incorrect. $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is not a self-indicator. The intense blue colour comes from the indicator diphenylamine, which dichromate oxidises just after the equivalence point.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the reaction between metallic copper and aqueous silver nitrate is INCORRECT?
options: The solution gradually develops a blue colour
Copper is oxidised to $Cu^{2+}$ by losing electrons
$Ag^{+}$ acts as the reducing agent in the reaction
The equilibrium greatly favours $Cu^{2+}(aq)$ and Ag(s)
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the $Cu^{2+}$ ions formed make the solution blue.
(2) Correct: Cu loses 2 electrons and becomes $Cu^{2+}$.
(3) Incorrect: $Ag^{+}$ accepts electrons and is reduced to Ag, so it is the oxidising agent, not the reducing agent. Cu is the reductant.
(4) Correct: NCERT states that the equilibrium greatly favours the products.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following metals displaces hydrogen from cold water?
options: Magnesium
Iron
Calcium
Silver
questions.explanation:
NCERT: all alkali metals and some alkaline earth metals (Ca, Sr, Ba) are very good reductants and displace $H_2$ from cold water. An example is $Ca + 2H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2 + H_2$.
Mg and Fe are less active and need steam to release $H_2$, so Mg is the tempting but wrong choice.
Ag does not react even with hydrochloric acid.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When excess KI solution is added to a solution containing Cu$^{2+}$ ions in iodometric estimation, the products formed are:
options: CuI$_2$ and I$^-$
Cu metal and I$_2$
Cu$_2$O and KI$_3$
questions.explanation:
NCERT reaction: 2Cu$^{2+}$ + 4I$^-$ → Cu$_2$I$_2$(s) + I$_2$.
Copper is reduced from +2 to +1 in Cu$_2$I$_2$, and iodide is oxidised to I$_2$.
Option (1) fails because CuI$_2$ is not a product; Cu(II) does not survive in the presence of I$^-$.
Option (2) fails because copper is not reduced all the way to the metal.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The reaction $2Na(s) + H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NaH(s)$ can be shown to be a redox change by writing the product as $Na^+H^-$ and splitting the reaction into two half reactions.
Statement II: In NaH, hydrogen carries an oxidation number of +1, as it does in most of its compounds.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The half reactions $2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-$ and $H_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2H^-$ show Na is oxidised and H is reduced.
Statement II is incorrect. In binary metal hydrides such as NaH, LiH and $CaH_2$, hydrogen is $-1$, not +1.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction):
List-I
(A) $V_2O_5 + 5Ca \rightarrow 2V + 5CaO$
(B) $2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$
(C) $P_4 + 3OH^- + 3H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_2PO_2^-$
(D) $3Mg + N_2 \rightarrow Mg_3N_2$
List-II
(i) Combination
(ii) Decomposition
(iii) Metal displacement
(iv) Disproportionation
options: A-iii, B-ii, C-iv, D-i
A-ii, B-iii, C-i, D-iv
A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i
A-i, B-ii, C-iv, D-iii
questions.explanation:
(A) Ca displaces V from $V_2O_5$ (V goes from +5 to 0), so this is metal displacement (iii).
(B) One compound breaks into KCl and elemental $O_2$, so this is decomposition (ii).
(C) P goes from 0 to –3 in $PH_3$ and to +1 in $H_2PO_2^-$, so this is disproportionation (iv).
(D) Two elements combine into one compound, so this is combination (i).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phosphorus belongs to group 15 of the long form of the periodic table. What is the highest oxidation number it can show, as seen in $P_4O_{10}$?
questions.explanation:
For a representative element beyond groups 1 and 2, the highest oxidation number equals the group number minus 10.
For phosphorus this gives 15 − 10 = +5.
Check with $P_4O_{10}$: 4x + 10(−2) = 0, so x = +5.
+3 is a common lower state of phosphorus, not its maximum. +15 would wrongly use the group number directly.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reduction process) with List-II (classical basis for calling it reduction):
List-I
A. $2HgO \rightarrow 2Hg + O_2$ (HgO reduced)
B. $2FeCl_3 + H_2 \rightarrow 2FeCl_2 + 2HCl$ (FeCl3 reduced)
C. $CH_2=CH_2 + H_2 \rightarrow H_3C-CH_3$ (ethene reduced)
D. $2HgCl_2 + SnCl_2 \rightarrow Hg_2Cl_2 + SnCl_4$ (HgCl2 reduced)
List-II
(i) Removal of oxygen
(ii) Addition of hydrogen
(iii) Addition of an electropositive element
(iv) Removal of an electronegative element
options: A-(i), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(iii)
A-(i), B-(ii), C-(iv), D-(iii)
A-(iv), B-(i), C-(ii), D-(iii)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
A: Mercuric oxide loses oxygen, which is (i).
B: Ferric chloride loses chlorine, an electronegative element, which is (iv).
C: Ethene gains hydrogen, which is (ii).
D: Mercury, an electropositive element, is effectively added to HgCl2, giving Hg2Cl2. This is (iii).
Answer: (1)
