questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given the standard electrode potentials at 298 K: $E^\circ(Cl_2/Cl^-) = 1.36$ V, $E^\circ(Br_2/Br^-) = 1.09$ V, $E^\circ(Ag^+/Ag) = 0.80$ V, $E^\circ(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = 0.77$ V, $E^\circ(I_2/I^-) = 0.54$ V, $E^\circ(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = 0.34$ V, $E^\circ(Zn^{2+}/Zn) = -0.76$ V.
How many of the following reactions are feasible under standard conditions?
(i) $Cl_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + Br_2$
(ii) $I_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2I^- + Br_2$
(iii) $Zn + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + Cu$
(iv) $2Fe^{2+} + I_2 \rightarrow 2Fe^{3+} + 2I^-$
(v) $2Ag + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow 2Ag^+ + Cu$
questions.explanation:
Rule: a reaction is feasible if the species being reduced belongs to the couple with the higher $E^\circ$.
(i) Feasible: $Cl_2$ (1.36 V) can oxidise $Br^-$ (1.09 V).
(ii) Not feasible: $I_2$ (0.54 V) is a weaker oxidant than $Br_2$ (1.09 V).
(iii) Feasible: Zn (−0.76 V) is a stronger reductant than Cu (0.34 V).
(iv) Not feasible: $Fe^{3+}$ (0.77 V) is the stronger oxidant, so the reverse reaction occurs.
(v) Not feasible: $Ag^+/Ag$ (0.80 V) lies above $Cu^{2+}/Cu$ (0.34 V), so Ag cannot reduce $Cu^{2+}$.
Two reactions are feasible.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are disproportionation reactions?
(i) $Cl_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow ClO^- + Cl^- + H_2O$
(ii) $2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$
(iii) $2NO_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow NO_2^- + NO_3^- + H_2O$
(iv) $2F_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow 2F^- + OF_2 + H_2O$
(v) $3ClO^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + ClO_3^-$
(vi) $2Pb(NO_3)_2 \rightarrow 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2$
questions.explanation:
(i) Yes: Cl goes from 0 to −1 and +1.
(ii) No: Cl is reduced (+5 to −1) but a different element, O, is oxidised (−2 to 0).
(iii) Yes: N goes from +4 to +3 and +5.
(iv) No: F is only reduced (0 to −1); O is oxidised (−2 to +2).
(v) Yes: Cl goes from +1 to −1 and +5.
(vi) No: N is reduced and O is oxidised, so this is a decomposition redox reaction.
That gives 3 disproportionation reactions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Permanganate ion oxidises bromide ion in basic medium to bromate ion and is itself reduced to $\mathrm{MnO_2}$. Which of the following is the correctly balanced ionic equation?
options: $\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + Br^- + H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + BrO_3^- + 2OH^-}$
$\mathrm{MnO_4^- + Br^- + H_2O \rightarrow MnO_2 + BrO_3^- + 2OH^-}$
$\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + Br^- + 2H^+ \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + BrO_3^- + H_2O}$
$\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + 3Br^- + 4H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + 3BrO_3^- + 8OH^-}$
questions.explanation:
Mn goes from +7 to +4, a decrease of 3. Br goes from –1 to +5, an increase of 6.
To equalise the changes, take 2 $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ for every 1 $\mathrm{Br^-}$.
Charge is –3 on the left and –1 on the right, so add 2 $\mathrm{OH^-}$ on the right (the medium is basic, so $\mathrm{H^+}$ is not used).
H balance then needs 1 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ on the left. O check: 9 on each side.
Option (2) has the wrong electron balance, and option (3) uses $\mathrm{H^+}$ in a basic medium.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the oxidation number of hydrogen in barium hydride, $BaH_2$?
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen is normally +1. The exception is a binary compound in which hydrogen is bonded to a metal.
Ba is an alkaline earth metal, so it is +2.
Sum rule: $+2 + 2x = 0$, which gives $x = -1$.
The option +1 is tempting, but it ignores the metal-hydride exception.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In how many of the following species does the indicated element have an oxidation number of exactly +6?
Cr in $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$; Mn in $MnO_4^{2-}$; S in $SF_6$; S in $SO_3$; Mn in $MnO_4^-$; Br (average) in $Br_3O_8$; S (average) in $S_4O_6^{2-}$
questions.explanation:
Cr: 2x – 14 = –2 gives x = +6. Yes.
Mn in $MnO_4^{2-}$: x – 8 = –2 gives x = +6. Yes.
S in $SF_6$: +6 (the highest state for group 16). Yes.
S in $SO_3$: +6. Yes.
Mn in $MnO_4^-$: +7. No.
Br average in $Br_3O_8$: 16/3. No.
S average in $S_4O_6^{2-}$: 2.5. No.
Total = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the copper redox couple of the Daniell cell, following the NCERT convention?
options: $Cu/Cu^{2+}$, because the reduced form is written first
$Cu^{2+}/Cu$, because the oxidised form is written before the reduced form
$Cu^{2+}/Cu$, because the species with the higher mass is written first
$Cu/Cu^{2+}$, because the solid phase is always written before the solution
questions.explanation:
A redox couple contains both the oxidised and the reduced form of a substance taking part in a half reaction.
The two forms are separated by a slash or vertical line, which represents the interface.
By convention the oxidised form is put first, so the couples are written $Zn^{2+}/Zn$ and $Cu^{2+}/Cu$.
Option (3) gives the right notation for the wrong reason, since mass plays no role.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $2Na(s) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2NaCl(s)$, which half reaction represents the oxidation step?
options: $Cl_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-$
$Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na$
$2Cl^- \rightarrow Cl_2 + 2e^-$
$2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-$
questions.explanation:
NaCl is ionic, $Na^+Cl^-$, so sodium must lose electrons and chlorine must gain them.
Oxidation is loss of electrons, so the oxidation half is $2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-$.
$Cl_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-$ is the reduction half. It is the tempting choice, but it shows a gain of electrons.
Options (2) and (3) describe the reverse processes, which do not occur here.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A sample of pure sodium oxalate, Na$_2$C$_2$O$_4$, is dissolved in dilute H$_2$SO$_4$ and titrated with 0.0200 M KMnO$_4$. The first permanent pink tinge appears after 20.0 mL of KMnO$_4$ is added. In acid, MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$ and oxalate is oxidised to CO$_2$. What is the mass of sodium oxalate in the sample? (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation:
Given: mol MnO$_4^-$ = 0.0200 L × 0.0200 M = 4.00 × 10$^{-4}$ mol.
Electron count: Mn goes +7 → +2, gaining 5 e$^-$. Each C goes +3 → +4, so oxalate loses 2 e$^-$. The mole ratio is MnO$_4^-$ : C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ = 2 : 5.
Substituting: mol oxalate = 4.00 × 10$^{-4}$ × 5/2 = 1.00 × 10$^{-3}$ mol.
Molar mass of Na$_2$C$_2$O$_4$ = 46 + 24 + 64 = 134 g/mol.
So mass = 1.00 × 10$^{-3}$ × 134 = 0.134 g.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In how many of the following does the specified atom have an oxidation number of exactly $-1$?
H in $LiH$; O in $BaO_2$; F in $OF_2$; Cl in $HOCl$; O in $KO_2$; Br in $NaBr$
questions.explanation:
H in LiH: −1 (metal hydride). Counts.
O in $BaO_2$: −1 (peroxide). Counts.
F in $OF_2$: −1 (fluorine is −1 in all its compounds). Counts.
Cl in HOCl: +1 (halogen bonded to oxygen). Does not count.
O in $KO_2$: $-\frac{1}{2}$ (superoxide). Does not count.
Br in NaBr: −1 (halide ion). Counts.
Total = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about indicators in redox titrations is INCORRECT?
options: $MnO_4^-$ acts as a self-indicator; the first lasting pink tinge marks the end point
$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ acts as a self-indicator, and its own colour change marks the end point
In the titration of iodine liberated by $Cu^{2+}$, the blue starch–iodine colour disappears when thiosulphate has consumed all the iodine
Iodine, though insoluble in water, stays in solution in the presence of KI as $KI_3$
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: intensely coloured $MnO_4^-$ signals the end point by itself.
(2) Incorrect: NCERT states that $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is not a self-indicator. Just after the equivalence point it oxidises diphenylamine, which gives an intense blue colour.
(3) Correct: $I_2 + 2S_2O_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2I^- + S_4O_6^{2-}$ removes the iodine, so the blue colour vanishes.
(4) Correct: $I_2$ dissolves in KI solution as $KI_3$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The average oxidation number of sulphur in $Na_2S_2O_3$ is $+2$
The oxidation number of chromium in $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is $+6$
The oxidation number of chlorine in $HClO_4$ is $+7$
The oxidation number of oxygen in $OF_2$ is $-2$
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $2(+1) + 2x + 3(-2) = 0$, so $x = +2$ (an average value).
(2) Correct: $2x + 7(-2) = -2$, so $x = +6$.
(3) Correct: $+1 + x - 8 = 0$, so $x = +7$.
(4) Incorrect: F is always −1, so in $OF_2$ oxygen is $+2$, not $-2$.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about redox titrations is correct?
options: Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ acts as a self-indicator just like MnO$_4^-$
Diphenylamine is oxidised by Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ just after the equivalence point, giving an intense blue colour
The equivalence point is the point where equal volumes of oxidant and reductant solutions have been mixed
In dichromate titrations, the end point is seen as the first lasting pink colour
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: dichromate shows no dramatic colour change of its own, so it is not a self-indicator.
(2) Correct: diphenylamine is oxidised by Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ just after the equivalence point, producing an intense blue colour.
(3) Incorrect: the equivalence point is where oxidant and reductant are equal in mole stoichiometry, not in volume.
(4) Incorrect: the lasting pink end point belongs to permanganate titrations.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match each balanced reaction in List-I with the total number of electrons transferred in it (as written) in List-II.
List-I
(A) $\mathrm{6Fe^{2+} + Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ \rightarrow 6Fe^{3+} + 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O}$
(B) $\mathrm{H_2O_2 + 2Fe^{2+} + 2H^+ \rightarrow 2Fe^{3+} + 2H_2O}$
(C) $\mathrm{P_4 + 3OH^- + 3H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_2PO_2^-}$
(D) $\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + 5SO_2 + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 5HSO_4^-}$
List-II
(I) 2
(II) 3
(III) 6
(IV) 10
options: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
questions.explanation:
(A) 6 Fe atoms each change from +2 to +3, so 6 electrons are transferred → III.
(B) In $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$, 2 O atoms each change from –1 to –2, so 2 electrons are transferred → I.
(C) One P goes from 0 to –3 (gains 3). Three P atoms each go from 0 to +1 (lose 3 in total). So 3 electrons are transferred → II.
(D) 2 Mn atoms each change from +7 to +2, so 10 electrons are transferred → IV.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the reaction $MnO_4^- + SO_2 \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + HSO_4^-$ in acidic solution.
Statement I: In the balanced equation, the mole ratio $MnO_4^- : SO_2$ is 2 : 5.
Statement II: In the balanced equation, two water molecules appear on the product side.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Mn goes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons. S goes from +4 to +6, a loss of 2 electrons. So the ratio $MnO_4^- : SO_2$ is 2 : 5, and Statement I is correct.
The balanced equation is $2MnO_4^- + 5SO_2 + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 5HSO_4^-$.
Check: O is 20 on each side, H is 5 on each side, charge is −1 on each side.
The water appears on the reactant side, so Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following species undergo oxidation according to the classical definition in the reaction written against them?
(a) Mg in $Mg + Cl_2 \rightarrow MgCl_2$
(b) HgO in $2HgO \rightarrow 2Hg + O_2$
(c) H2S in $2H_2S + O_2 \rightarrow 2S + 2H_2O$
(d) Ethene in $CH_2=CH_2 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6$
(e) SnCl2 in $2HgCl_2 + SnCl_2 \rightarrow Hg_2Cl_2 + SnCl_4$
(f) S in $S + O_2 \rightarrow SO_2$
questions.explanation:
(a) Oxidised: the electronegative element Cl is added to Mg.
(b) Not oxidised: HgO loses oxygen, so it is reduced.
(c) Oxidised: hydrogen is removed from H2S.
(d) Not oxidised: ethene gains hydrogen, so it is reduced.
(e) Oxidised: chlorine is added, converting SnCl2 to SnCl4.
(f) Oxidised: oxygen is added to S.
That gives 4 oxidations.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
White phosphorus reacts with alkali: $P_4(s) + OH^- + H_2O \rightarrow PH_3(g) + H_2PO_2^-$ (unbalanced). Consider the following statements about the balanced equation with the smallest whole-number coefficients:
(i) $P_4$ acts as both oxidant and reductant.
(ii) The ratio of P atoms oxidised to P atoms reduced is 3 : 1.
(iii) A total of 3 electrons is transferred per $P_4$ molecule.
(iv) The coefficient of $OH^-$ is 3.
(v) Water appears on the product side.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Balanced equation: $P_4 + 3OH^- + 3H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_2PO_2^-$.
(i) Correct: P goes from 0 to −3 and also from 0 to +1, so this is disproportionation.
(ii) Correct: 3 P atoms go to +1 and 1 P atom goes to −3.
(iii) Correct: 3 P atoms each lose 1 electron, and these 3 electrons are gained by the one P that becomes −3.
(iv) Correct: the coefficient of $OH^-$ is 3.
(v) Incorrect: water is a reactant.
So four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about indicators in redox titrations is INCORRECT?
options: $MnO_4^-$ acts as a self indicator; the end point is the first lasting pink tinge after all the reductant is oxidised
$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ acts as a self indicator in its titration with $Fe^{2+}$, as its orange colour sharply disappears at the end point
In the iodometric estimation of $Cu^{2+}$, the blue colour of starch-iodine disappears when the liberated iodine is consumed by thiosulphate
Iodine, though insoluble in water, stays in solution containing KI in the form of $KI_3$
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: intensely coloured $MnO_4^-$ is its own indicator. A pink tinge appears at very low concentration.
(2) Incorrect: NCERT states that $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is NOT a self indicator. Just after the equivalence point it oxidises diphenylamine, giving an intense blue colour.
(3) Correct: $I_2$ gives a blue colour with starch, which vanishes as $S_2O_3^{2-}$ converts $I_2$ to $I^-$.
(4) Correct: iodine dissolves as $KI_3$ in KI solution.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ammonia is oxidised by oxygen as $\mathrm{4NH_3(g) + 5O_2(g) \rightarrow 4NO(g) + 6H_2O(g)}$. If 8.5 g of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is reacted with 16.0 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$, what is the maximum mass of NO formed? (Atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation:
Given: moles of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ = 8.5/17 = 0.50 mol; moles of $\mathrm{O_2}$ = 16/32 = 0.50 mol.
Formula: 4 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$ needs 5 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$, so 0.50 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$ would need 0.625 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$. Only 0.50 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$ is available, so $\mathrm{O_2}$ is the limiting reagent.
Substituting: moles of NO = 0.50 × 4/5 = 0.40 mol; mass of NO = 0.40 × 30 = 12.0 g.
The option 15.0 g assumes $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is limiting.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation number of $-1$?
options: $HCl$
$CaH_2$
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen is normally +1.
It becomes $-1$ when it is bonded to a metal in a binary compound (a metal hydride).
$CaH_2$ is a binary hydride of the alkaline earth metal calcium. Ca is +2, so each H is $-1$.
In $HCl$, $NH_3$ and $H_2O$, hydrogen is bonded to non-metals that are more electronegative than it, so H is +1 in all three.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
options: $2H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2 + O_2$
$2NaH \rightarrow 2Na + H_2$
$2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$
$CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$
questions.explanation:
A decomposition is redox only if some element changes its oxidation number. This usually happens when at least one product is an element.
In $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$, Ca stays +2, C stays +4 and O stays –2, so nothing is oxidised or reduced.
In the other three reactions an element is formed. $H_2$ and $O_2$ form from water, Na and $H_2$ form from NaH, and $O_2$ forms from $KClO_3$. In each of these, oxidation numbers change.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the half-reaction (ion-electron) method, a redox reaction occurring in basic medium is first balanced as if it were in acidic medium. What is the correct next step?
options: Replace every $H^+$ by an electron
Add as many $OH^-$ ions to both sides as there are $H^+$ ions, and combine $H^+$ and $OH^-$ on the same side into $H_2O$
Add $OH^-$ ions only to the side containing $H^+$ and delete water molecules
Multiply the whole equation by 2 and cancel all $H^+$
questions.explanation:
NCERT rule: for each $H^+$, add an equal number of $OH^-$ to both sides of the equation.
Where $H^+$ and $OH^-$ appear on the same side, they combine to give $H_2O$. Any excess water is then cancelled.
Adding $OH^-$ to one side only would destroy the atom and charge balance, so option (3) fails.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the decomposition $2H_2O_2(aq) \rightarrow 2H_2O(l) + O_2(g)$, the oxidation number of oxygen changes from:
options: $-1$ to $-2$ only
questions.explanation:
In the peroxide $H_2O_2$, each oxygen atom has oxidation number $-1$.
In $H_2O$, oxygen is $-2$, so this oxygen is reduced.
In $O_2$, oxygen is $0$, so this oxygen is oxidised.
The same element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced, so this is disproportionation.
Option (3) misses the oxidation to $O_2$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fluorine gas cannot be prepared by oxidising fluoride ions with any chemical reagent; it is obtained only by electrolytic oxidation.
Reason (R): Fluorine is the strongest oxidising agent, so no chemical species can remove electrons from $F^-$.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that the only way to obtain F2 from F– is electrolytic oxidation.
R is true. F2 is the strongest oxidising agent, with the highest $E^\circ$ = 2.87 V.
R explains A. Oxidising F– would need an oxidant stronger than F2, and no such chemical oxidant exists.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the electron-transfer concept, an oxidising agent is a species that:
options: donates electrons to another species
accepts electrons from another species
loses electrons and is itself oxidised
accepts protons from another species
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines an oxidising agent as an acceptor of electrons.
By accepting electrons, it causes the other species to be oxidised, while it is itself reduced.
Donating electrons, or losing them and being oxidised, describes a reducing agent.
Accepting protons describes a base, not an oxidant.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Permanganate oxidises sulphite in basic medium according to the skeletal equation
$MnO_4^- + SO_3^{2-} \rightarrow MnO_2 + SO_4^{2-}$
After balancing with the smallest whole-number coefficients, how many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The mole ratio $MnO_4^- : SO_3^{2-}$ is 2 : 3.
(ii) Two $OH^-$ ions appear on the product side.
(iii) One $H_2O$ molecule appears on the reactant side.
(iv) A total of 6 electrons are transferred in the balanced equation.
(v) Manganese is oxidised in this reaction.
questions.explanation:
Mn goes from +7 to +4 (gains 3 e⁻). S goes from +4 to +6 (loses 2 e⁻).
Equalising electrons: 2 Mn and 3 S, so 6 e⁻ are transferred.
The balanced equation is $2MnO_4^- + 3SO_3^{2-} + H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + 3SO_4^{2-} + 2OH^-$. Charge is –8 on each side, and O is 18 on each side.
So (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
(v) is wrong: Mn is reduced.
Total = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the compound in List-I with the oxidation number of oxygen in List-II.
List-I
(A) $H_2O_2$
(B) $KO_2$
(C) $O_2F_2$
(D) $OF_2$
List-II
(i) $+2$
(ii) $-\frac{1}{2}$
(iii) $+1$
(iv) $-1$
options: A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(i), B-(iii), C-(ii), D-(iv)
questions.explanation:
(A) $H_2O_2$ is a peroxide: 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so O = $-1$, which is (iv).
(B) $KO_2$ is a superoxide: +1 + 2x = 0, so O = $-\frac{1}{2}$, which is (ii).
(C) $O_2F_2$: 2x + 2(−1) = 0, so O = +1, which is (iii).
(D) $OF_2$: x + 2(−1) = 0, so O = +2, which is (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the Stock-notation name with its formula?
options: Thallium(I) sulphate – $TlSO_4$
Iron(III) sulphate – $Fe_2(SO_4)_3$
Chromium(III) oxide – $CrO_3$
Tin(IV) oxide – $SnO$
questions.explanation:
The Roman numeral gives the metal's oxidation number. Balance it against sulphate ($-2$) or oxide ($-2$).
(1) Wrong: Tl(I) needs two Tl per sulphate, so the formula is $Tl_2SO_4$.
(2) Correct: $2(+3) + 3(-2) = 0$, so the formula is $Fe_2(SO_4)_3$.
(3) Wrong: Cr in $CrO_3$ is $+6$. Chromium(III) oxide is $Cr_2O_3$.
(4) Wrong: Sn in $SnO$ is $+2$. Tin(IV) oxide is $SnO_2$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ammonia is oxidised by oxygen according to $4NH_3(g) + 5O_2(g) \rightarrow 4NO(g) + 6H_2O(g)$. What is the maximum mass of NO that can be obtained from 8.5 g of $NH_3$ and 16 g of $O_2$? (Atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation:
Given: moles of $NH_3$ = 8.5/17 = 0.5 mol; moles of $O_2$ = 16/32 = 0.5 mol.
To react 0.5 mol $NH_3$ needs $0.5 \times \frac{5}{4} = 0.625$ mol $O_2$. Only 0.5 mol is available, so $O_2$ is the limiting reagent.
Moles of NO formed = $0.5 \times \frac{4}{5} = 0.4$ mol.
Mass of NO = $0.4 \times 30$ = 12 g.
The 15 g option wrongly treats $NH_3$ as the limiting reagent.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following metals can liberate dihydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid?
Zn, Mg, Fe, Cd, Sn, Ag, Au
questions.explanation:
Zn, Mg and Fe all react with HCl to give $H_2$. NCERT uses these reactions for the laboratory preparation of dihydrogen.
Cd and Sn do not react even with steam, yet they still displace $H_2$ from acids.
Ag and Au are very less active metals that can occur native. They do not react even with HCl.
So the count is 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given the standard electrode potentials (V):
$Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+} = 0.77$, $I_2/I^- = 0.54$, $Br_2/Br^- = 1.09$, $Cl_2/Cl^- = 1.36$, $Cu^{2+}/Cu = 0.34$, $Ag^+/Ag = 0.80$, $Zn^{2+}/Zn = -0.76$, $Ni^{2+}/Ni = -0.25$.
How many of the following species can be oxidised by $Fe^{3+}(aq)$ under standard conditions?
$I^-$, $Br^-$, $Cu$, $Ag$, $Zn$, $Ni$, $Cl^-$
questions.explanation:
Fe³⁺ (0.77 V) can oxidise the reduced form of any couple with a lower $E^\circ$.
I⁻ (0.54 V): yes.
Cu (0.34 V): yes.
Zn (−0.76 V): yes.
Ni (−0.25 V): yes.
Br⁻ (1.09 V) and Cl⁻ (1.36 V): no, these couples lie higher.
Ag (0.80 V): no. 0.80 V is slightly above 0.77 V, so Fe³⁺ cannot oxidise silver.
Total: 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For an electrode potential to be called a standard electrode potential, certain conditions must be met. Which of the following is NOT one of these conditions?
options: Each species taking part in the electrode reaction has unit concentration
Any gas involved in the electrode reaction is at 1 atm pressure
The reaction is carried out at 298 K
The electrolyte solution is kept at pH 7
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines standard conditions in three parts: unit concentration of each species, 1 atm pressure for any gas, and a temperature of 298 K.
Options (1), (2) and (3) are exactly these conditions.
A neutral pH is not a requirement. The standard hydrogen electrode itself needs $H^+$ at unit concentration, which is far from pH 7.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Unlike chlorine, fluorine does not undergo disproportionation when it reacts with alkali.
Reason (R): Being the most electronegative element, fluorine cannot exhibit any positive oxidation state.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $2F_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow 2F^- + OF_2 + H_2O$. Here F goes only from 0 to −1. Oxygen (from −2 to +2 in $OF_2$) is the species oxidised.
R is true. To disproportionate, fluorine would have to reach a higher state than 0 as well as a lower one. Since it cannot take a positive state, it cannot be oxidised and reduced simultaneously.
So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to NCERT, a redox couple with a negative standard electrode potential ($E^\circ$) is
options: a stronger oxidising agent than the $H^+/H_2$ couple
a weaker reducing agent than the $H^+/H_2$ couple
a stronger reducing agent than the $H^+/H_2$ couple
unable to take part in any redox reaction
questions.explanation:
The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned $E^\circ = 0.00$ V by convention.
A negative $E^\circ$ means the couple is a stronger reducing agent than $H^+/H_2$.
A positive $E^\circ$ means it is a weaker reducing agent.
For example, $Li^+/Li$ ($-3.05$ V) lies at the bottom of Table 7.1, so Li is the strongest reductant in the table.
Option (2) states the meaning of a positive $E^\circ$, not a negative one.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following halogen displacement reactions does NOT occur in aqueous solution?
options: $Cl_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + I_2$
$Br_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Br^- + I_2$
$Cl_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + Br_2$
$Br_2 + 2Cl^- \rightarrow 2Br^- + Cl_2$
questions.explanation:
Oxidising power decreases down group 17: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.
A halogen can only displace a halide ion that lies below it in the group.
$Cl_2$ displaces $Br^-$ and $I^-$, and $Br_2$ displaces $I^-$, so reactions (1)–(3) occur.
$Br_2$ is a weaker oxidant than $Cl_2$, so it cannot oxidise $Cl^-$.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrazine reacts with chlorate ion in basic medium: $N_2H_4(l) + ClO_3^-(aq) \rightarrow NO(g) + Cl^-(aq)$. When this is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, which statement is correct?
options: 6 molecules of $H_2O$ are formed, and no $OH^-$ appears in the final equation
4 $OH^-$ ions appear on the reactant side
A total of 12 electrons is transferred in the balanced equation
The mole ratio $N_2H_4 : ClO_3^-$ is 4 : 3
questions.explanation:
N goes from −2 to +2, an increase of 4 per N, or 8 per $N_2H_4$. Cl goes from +5 to −1, a decrease of 6.
The LCM of 8 and 6 is 24, giving $3N_2H_4 + 4ClO_3^- \rightarrow 6NO + 4Cl^-$.
O is 12 on the left and 6 on the right, so add 6 $H_2O$ to the right. H is then 12 on each side and charge is −4 on each side, so no $OH^-$ is needed.
Therefore 24 electrons are transferred, and the ratio $N_2H_4 : ClO_3^-$ is 3 : 4.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conversion $2K_4[Fe(CN)_6] + H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2K_3[Fe(CN)_6] + 2KOH$ is interpreted as oxidation of potassium ferrocyanide in the classical sense because:
options: oxygen is added to the ferrocyanide ion
hydrogen is removed from potassium ferrocyanide
the electropositive element potassium is removed from it
the electronegative element nitrogen is removed from it
questions.explanation:
K4[Fe(CN)6] becomes K3[Fe(CN)6], so one potassium is lost per formula unit.
Potassium is an electropositive element.
Removal of an electropositive element counts as oxidation in the broadened classical definition.
No oxygen is added to the complex, and it contains no hydrogen to lose.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A copper wire is dipped in excess silver nitrate solution. During the reaction, 0.635 g of copper dissolves. What mass of silver is deposited? (Cu = 63.5, Ag = 108 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
Given: 0.635 g of Cu reacts; Cu = 63.5 g/mol; Ag = 108 g/mol.
Reaction: $Cu(s) + 2Ag^{+}(aq) \to Cu^{2+}(aq) + 2Ag(s)$.
Moles of Cu = $\frac{0.635}{63.5}$ = 0.01 mol. Each Cu atom gives 2 electrons, so 0.02 mol of Ag is deposited.
Mass of Ag = 0.02 × 108 = 2.16 g.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction $H_2S(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g) + S(s)$, which of the following statements is INCORRECT according to the classical idea of redox?
options: H2S is oxidised because the more electronegative element chlorine is added to its hydrogen
H2S is oxidised because the more electropositive element hydrogen is removed from sulphur
Sulphur is reduced because hydrogen is removed from it
Chlorine is reduced because hydrogen is added to it
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Cl becomes attached to H, which is addition of an electronegative element.
(2) Correct: electropositive H is removed from S, which also counts as oxidation.
(3) Incorrect: removal of hydrogen means oxidation, so sulphur is oxidised, not reduced.
(4) Correct: Cl2 becomes HCl, so hydrogen is added to chlorine, which is reduction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one of the following oxoanions of chlorine cannot undergo a disproportionation reaction?
options: $ClO^-$
questions.explanation:
In a disproportionation reaction, the element must be in an intermediate oxidation state so that it can be both oxidised and reduced.
Chlorine is +1 in $ClO^-$, +3 in $ClO_2^-$ and +5 in $ClO_3^-$. These are all intermediate states, so these ions can disproportionate.
In $ClO_4^-$, chlorine is +7, its highest oxidation state. It cannot be oxidised further, so it cannot disproportionate.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Metallic cobalt is placed in nickel sulphate solution: $Co(s) + Ni^{2+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons Co^{2+}(aq) + Ni(s)$. What do chemical tests show at equilibrium?
options: Only $Co^{2+}$ is present; the reaction goes to completion
Only $Ni^{2+}$ is present; no reaction occurs
Both $Ni^{2+}$ and $Co^{2+}$ are present at moderate concentrations
Both metals dissolve completely, leaving no solid
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that at equilibrium both $Ni^{2+}(aq)$ and $Co^{2+}(aq)$ are present at moderate concentrations.
So neither the reactants [Co(s) and $Ni^{2+}$] nor the products [$Co^{2+}$ and Ni(s)] are greatly favoured.
This is unlike the Zn/$Cu^{2+}$ reaction, where the products are strongly favoured.
Options (1) and (2) describe the two extreme cases, which do not apply here.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following give a fractional value when the oxidation number of the indicated element is calculated by the usual rules?
$C_3O_2$ (C), $Br_3O_8$ (Br), $Na_2S_4O_6$ (S), $Fe_3O_4$ (Fe), $Mn_3O_4$ (Mn), $Pb_3O_4$ (Pb), $KI_3$ (I), $H_2SO_5$ (S), $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ (Cr), $NO_3^-$ (N)
questions.explanation:
Fractional values:
- C in $C_3O_2$: 4/3
- Br in $Br_3O_8$: 16/3
- S in $Na_2S_4O_6$: 2.5
- Fe, Mn and Pb in $M_3O_4$: 8/3 each
- I in $KI_3$: −1/3

Whole-number values: S in $H_2SO_5$ (+6 by structure, +8 by naive calculation), Cr in $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ (+6) and N in $NO_3^-$ (+5).
Total fractional = 7.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Standard reduction potentials at 298 K are:
$MnO_4^-/Mn^{2+}$ (acidic) = 1.51 V; $Cl_2/Cl^-$ = 1.36 V; $Cr_2O_7^{2-}/Cr^{3+}$ (acidic) = 1.33 V; $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}$ = 0.77 V; $I_2/I^-$ = 0.54 V.
Under standard conditions, which species can oxidise $Cl^-$ to $Cl_2$?
options: $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ in acidic medium
$MnO_4^-$ in acidic medium
questions.explanation:
To oxidise $Cl^-$, the oxidant's couple must have a higher reduction potential than $Cl_2/Cl^-$ (1.36 V).
Only $MnO_4^-/Mn^{2+}$ (1.51 V) is higher, so acidic permanganate can oxidise chloride.
$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is the tempting choice, but at 1.33 V it is just below 1.36 V.
$Fe^{3+}$ (0.77 V) and $I_2$ (0.54 V) are far weaker oxidants.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (species) with List-II (actual oxidation state picture of the indicated element).
List-I:
(A) Carbon in $C_3O_2$
(B) Sulphur in $S_4O_6^{2-}$
(C) Lead in $Pb_3O_4$
(D) Oxygen in $KO_2$
List-II:
(I) Each atom has the same value, $-\frac{1}{2}$
(II) Two atoms at +2 and one atom at 0
(III) Two atoms at +5 and two atoms at 0
(IV) Equivalent to 2 mol of the +2 state and 1 mol of the +4 state
options: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
questions.explanation:
(A) In O=C=C=C=O, the terminal carbons are +2 and the central carbon is 0 (average 4/3), so A-II.
(B) In tetrathionate, the end sulphurs are +5 and the middle two are 0 (average 2.5), so B-III.
(C) $Pb_3O_4$ is 2PbO·$PbO_2$, i.e. two Pb(II) and one Pb(IV), so C-IV.
(D) In the superoxide ion $O_2^-$, each O is $-\frac{1}{2}$. This fraction is genuine, not an average of different whole numbers, so D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bromine can liberate iodine from an aqueous solution of potassium iodide.
Reason (R): $Br_2$ and $I_2$ dissolve in $CCl_4$ to give coloured solutions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $Br_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Br^- + I_2$ occurs because $Br_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $I_2$. Oxidising power decreases from F to I down the group.
R is also true. This colour in $CCl_4$ is the basis of the layer test used to detect the liberated halogen.
However, R only describes how the product is detected. It does not explain why the displacement occurs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: A positive standard electrode potential ($E^\ominus$) means that the redox couple is a stronger reducing agent than the $H^+/H_2$ couple.
Statement II: In a Daniell cell, electrons flow through the external wire from the zinc rod to the copper rod.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. A positive $E^\ominus$ means the couple is a weaker reducing agent than $H^+/H_2$. A negative $E^\ominus$ means it is a stronger reducing agent.
Statement II is correct. Zn is oxidised at the anode. The electrons it releases travel through the wire to the copper rod, where they reduce $Cu^{2+}$ ions.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the reaction $2Na(s) + S(s) \rightarrow Na_2S(s)$, sulphur acts as the oxidising agent.
Reason (R): Sulphur donates two electrons to sodium atoms and forms the $S^{2-}$ ion.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
$Na_2S$ is ionic, $(Na^+)_2S^{2-}$, and its half reactions are $2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-$ and $S + 2e^- \rightarrow S^{2-}$.
A is true: sulphur accepts electrons, so it is the oxidising agent.
R is false: sulphur accepts, not donates, two electrons to form $S^{2-}$. A species that donated electrons could not become an anion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $Mn^{3+}$ is unstable in aqueous solution and disproportionates into $Mn^{2+}$, $MnO_2$ and $H^+$. In the balanced ionic equation with the smallest whole-number coefficients, the coefficients of $Mn^{3+}$ and $H^+$ are respectively:
options: 2 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 2
4 and 4
questions.explanation:
Oxidation: Mn goes from +3 to +4 in $MnO_2$, losing 1 e$^-$ per Mn.
Reduction: Mn goes from +3 to +2 in $Mn^{2+}$, gaining 1 e$^-$ per Mn.
Equal electrons need $2Mn^{3+} \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + MnO_2$.
Balance O by adding $2H_2O$ on the left, then balance H with $4H^+$ on the right.
This gives $2Mn^{3+} + 2H_2O \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + MnO_2 + 4H^+$.
Charge check: +6 on the left and +2 + 4 = +6 on the right.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 6.2 g of white phosphorus ($P_4$) is treated with excess hot aqueous NaOH. It disproportionates completely into phosphine ($PH_3$) and hypophosphite ion ($H_2PO_2^-$). What mass of phosphorus ends up in the hypophosphite ions? (Atomic mass of P = 31 u)
questions.explanation:
Given: P is 0 in $P_4$, −3 in $PH_3$ and +1 in $H_2PO_2^-$.
Balancing electrons: each P that is reduced gains 3 e⁻, and each P that is oxidised loses 1 e⁻. So 3 P are oxidised for every 1 P reduced: $P_4 + 3OH^- + 3H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_2PO_2^-$.
So $\frac{3}{4}$ of all P atoms go into hypophosphite.
Substituting: $\frac{3}{4} \times 6.2$ g = 4.65 g.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a copper strip is kept in zinc sulphate solution and $H_2S$ is then passed through the solution, no black CuS is formed, even though CuS is extremely insoluble.
Reason (R): The equilibrium for $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$ lies far towards the products.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that the CuS test is extremely sensitive because CuS is so insoluble, yet it detects no $Cu^{2+}$ in this experiment.
R is true. Zinc reduces $Cu^{2+}$ almost completely.
Cu in $Zn^{2+}$ solution is simply the reverse of this reaction. Since the forward reaction strongly favours the products, the reverse reaction forms only an undetectable trace of $Cu^{2+}$.
So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Peroxodisulphuric acid, $H_2S_2O_8$, contains one O–O linkage. A student assigns $-2$ to every oxygen and gets $+7$ for sulphur. What is the correct oxidation number of sulphur, and why was the student's value wrong?
options: $+7$; sulphur can exceed its group limit in peroxo acids
$+6$; the two peroxide oxygens are $-1$ each, and $+7$ exceeds the maximum for a group 16 element
$+5$; the peroxide oxygens are $-\frac{1}{2}$ each
$+8$; the O–O linkage adds one unit to each sulphur
questions.explanation:
The maximum oxidation number for sulphur (group 16) is $16 - 10 = +6$, so +7 is impossible.
The two oxygens in the O–O bond are peroxide oxygens (−1 each). The other six oxygens are −2.
Sum rule: $2(+1) + 2x + 2(-1) + 6(-2) = 0$, so $2x = 12$ and $x = +6$.
Option (3) wrongly uses the superoxide value for a peroxide link.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a Daniell cell, the zinc rod in $ZnSO_4$ solution and the copper rod in $CuSO_4$ solution are joined by a metallic wire, and the switch is turned on. Which statement correctly describes the external circuit?
options: Electrons flow from the zinc rod to the copper rod, and current flows from copper to zinc
Electrons flow from the copper rod to the zinc rod, and current flows from zinc to copper
Electrons and current both flow from the zinc rod to the copper rod
Electrons flow from zinc to copper only until the salt bridge saturates, then the flow reverses
questions.explanation:
Zinc is oxidised, $Zn \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + 2e^-$, so electrons are released at the zinc rod.
These electrons travel through the wire to the copper rod, where they reduce $Cu^{2+}$ to Cu.
NCERT notes that the direction of current is opposite to the direction of electron flow, so current flows from Cu to Zn.
Option (3) fails because current and electron flow cannot be in the same direction.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A sample of $CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O$ is dissolved in water and made up to 250 mL. A 25.0 mL portion is treated with excess KI: $2Cu^{2+} + 4I^- \rightarrow Cu_2I_2 + I_2$. The liberated iodine needs 20.0 mL of 0.100 M sodium thiosulphate: $I_2 + 2S_2O_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2I^- + S_4O_6^{2-}$. What mass of $CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O$ (molar mass 249.5 g/mol) was dissolved?
questions.explanation:
Given: thiosulphate used = 20.0 mL of 0.100 M = $2.00\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Formula: $2Cu^{2+} \equiv I_2 \equiv 2S_2O_3^{2-}$, so mol $Cu^{2+}$ = mol $S_2O_3^{2-}$ = $2.00\times10^{-3}$ mol in 25 mL.
Scaling to 250 mL: $2.00\times10^{-2}$ mol $Cu^{2+}$.
Substituting: mass = $0.0200 \times 249.5$ = 4.99 g.
So mass of $CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O$ = 4.99 g.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the estimation of $Cu^{2+}$ by adding excess $I^-$ and titrating with thiosulphate, the intense blue colour of starch disappears at the end point.
Reason (R): Iodine oxidises thiosulphate ions to sulphate ions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $Cu^{2+}$ liberates $I_2$ from $I^-$, and $I_2$ gives a blue colour with starch.
The blue colour vanishes once all the $I_2$ has been consumed by thiosulphate.
R is false. Iodine converts thiosulphate into tetrathionate: $I_2 + 2S_2O_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2I^- + S_4O_6^{2-}$. It does not give sulphate.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the oxidation number of the specified element in each species:
(i) Cr in $K_2Cr_2O_7$
(ii) S in $Na_2S_2O_3$ (average)
(iii) Mn in $BaMnO_4$
(iv) Cl in $KClO_3$
(v) S in $SF_6$
(vi) N in $NO_3^-$
In how many of these species is the oxidation number of the specified element equal to +6?
questions.explanation:
Use the sum rule with O = –2, F = –1, K and Na = +1, Ba = +2.
(i) 2 + 2x – 14 = 0, so x = +6. Counts.
(ii) 2 + 2x – 6 = 0, so x = +2 (average). Does not count.
(iii) 2 + x – 8 = 0, so x = +6. Counts.
(iv) 1 + x – 6 = 0, so x = +5. Does not count.
(v) x – 6 = 0, so x = +6. Counts.
(vi) x – 6 = –1, so x = +5. Does not count.
Three species, (i), (iii) and (v), have +6.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorite ion ($ClO_2^-$) disproportionates to give chlorate ($ClO_3^-$) and chloride ($Cl^-$) ions. What is the ratio of moles of $ClO_2^-$ oxidised to moles of $ClO_2^-$ reduced?
questions.explanation:
Chlorine is +3 in $ClO_2^-$.
Oxidation: +3 to +5 in $ClO_3^-$, which is a loss of 2 e$^-$ per ion.
Reduction: +3 to $-1$ in $Cl^-$, which is a gain of 4 e$^-$ per ion.
To balance electrons, 2 ions must be oxidised for every 1 ion reduced.
This matches NCERT's equation $6ClO_2^- \rightarrow 4ClO_3^- + 2Cl^-$, where 4 : 2 = 2 : 1.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute alkali as: $Cl_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow ClO^- + Cl^- + H_2O$. This reaction is used to make household bleaching agents. Which species is responsible for the bleaching action?
options: $Cl^-$ ion, which reduces coloured stains
$ClO^-$ ion, which oxidises coloured stains to colourless compounds
$OH^-$ ion, which neutralises coloured stains
$Cl_2$ molecule, which reduces coloured stains
questions.explanation:
In this reaction, chlorine (0) disproportionates into $Cl^-$ ($-1$) and $ClO^-$ ($+1$).
NCERT states that the hypochlorite ion oxidises the colour-bearing stains to colourless compounds.
$Cl^-$ is already in the lowest oxidation state and has no bleaching action.
Bleaching here is an oxidation, not a reduction or neutralisation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sulphur dioxide can act as an oxidising agent in some reactions and as a reducing agent in others.
Reason (R): The oxidation number of sulphur in $SO_2$ is $+4$, which lies between its lowest ($-2$) and highest ($+6$) oxidation numbers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: $SO_2$ can lose electrons (S goes to $+6$) or gain electrons (S goes to a lower state). So it acts as a reductant or an oxidant depending on the partner.
R is true: S in $SO_2$ is $+4$, an intermediate oxidation state.
R explains A: only a species with an intermediate oxidation number can be both raised and lowered.
By contrast, N in $HNO_3$ ($+5$) is in its highest state, so $HNO_3$ can act only as an oxidant.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the Daniell cell set-up, the beakers containing $ZnSO_4$ and $CuSO_4$ solutions are joined by a U-tube filled with KCl or $NH_4NO_3$ set in agar-agar jelly. What is the main role of this salt bridge?
options: It carries electrons from the zinc rod to the copper rod.
It provides electrical contact between the two solutions without letting them mix.
It supplies $Cu^{2+}$ ions to the cathode compartment so the reaction can continue.
It lets the $Cu^{2+}$ solution flow into the zinc beaker so that electrons transfer directly.
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the salt bridge connects the two solutions electrically while keeping them separate.
Inside the cell, the circuit is completed by ions moving through the bridge.
Electrons travel only through the external metallic wire, from Zn to Cu. Option (1) wrongly says the bridge carries electrons.
The KCl or $NH_4NO_3$ in the bridge does not supply $Cu^{2+}$, so option (3) is wrong.
If the solutions mixed, electrons would pass directly from Zn to $Cu^{2+}$ and no current would flow through the wire. So option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following compounds does oxygen have a positive oxidation number?
questions.explanation:
Fluorine is the most electronegative element and always has an oxidation number of –1. So when oxygen is bonded to fluorine, oxygen must be positive.
In $OF_2$: x + 2(–1) = 0, so x = +2.
In $Na_2O_2$, a peroxide, each O is –1.
In $KO_2$, a superoxide, each O is $-\frac{1}{2}$. This is unusual, but it is still negative, so it is the most tempting wrong choice.
In $H_2O$, O is the usual –2.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The competition among metals for releasing electrons is the basis of galvanic cells, in which a chemical reaction acts as the source of electrical energy.
(ii) Since Zn reduces $Cu^{2+}$ and Cu reduces $Ag^{+}$, zinc is expected to reduce $Ag^{+}$ ions in solution.
(iii) Metallic silver placed in zinc sulphate solution will deposit zinc.
(iv) Listing metals by their tendency to release electrons is similar to ranking acids by their tendency to release protons.
(v) Cobalt reduces $Ni^{2+}$ so strongly that the reaction goes practically to completion.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT links this competition for electrons to the design of galvanic cells.
(ii) Correct: the order Zn > Cu > Ag means Zn releases electrons more readily than Ag, so it can reduce $Ag^{+}$.
(iii) Incorrect: Ag is the weakest electron releaser of the three, so it cannot reduce $Zn^{2+}$.
(iv) Correct: NCERT draws this analogy with acid strength.
(v) Incorrect: in the Co/$Ni^{2+}$ system both ions remain at moderate concentrations.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the iodometric estimation of Cu$^{2+}$ are correct?
(i) Copper changes from +2 to +1 oxidation state when Cu$_2$I$_2$ forms.
(ii) Iodine, though insoluble in water, stays in solution containing KI as KI$_3$.
(iii) The blue colour of the starch–iodine complex appears at the end point of the thiosulphate titration.
(iv) The average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion formed is +2.5.
(v) The reaction between I$_2$ and thiosulphate is itself a redox reaction.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Cu$^{2+}$ → Cu(I) in Cu$_2$I$_2$.
(ii) Correct: I$_2$ is held in solution as KI$_3$.
(iii) Incorrect: the blue colour disappears at the end point, once thiosulphate has consumed all the iodine.
(iv) Correct: in S$_4$O$_6^{2-}$, 4x − 12 = −2, so x = +2.5.
(v) Correct: I$_2$ is reduced to I$^-$ and S is oxidised from +2 to +2.5.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following can act only as an oxidising agent and never as a reducing agent?
options: $HNO_3$
questions.explanation:
A species can act as both oxidant and reductant if its key element is in an intermediate oxidation state.
$SO_2$: S is +4, between −2 and +6, so it can act both ways.
$H_2O_2$: O is −1, between −2 and 0, so it can act both ways.
$NO_2$: N is +4, below its maximum of +5, so it can act both ways.
$HNO_3$: N is +5, the highest possible for a group 15 element. It can only decrease, so $HNO_3$ is only an oxidant.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the layer test, chlorine water is added to an aqueous solution of an unknown potassium halide, a little $CCl_4$ is added and the mixture is shaken. The $CCl_4$ layer turns violet. The halide ion present is:
questions.explanation:
Chlorine is a stronger oxidant than $Br_2$ and $I_2$. It oxidises $I^-$ to $I_2$: $Cl_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + I_2$.
$I_2$ dissolves in $CCl_4$ and gives a violet colour.
$Br^-$ would give $Br_2$, which colours the layer orange-brown, not violet.
$Cl_2$ cannot oxidise $Cl^-$ or $F^-$, so those give no colour.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given the standard electrode potentials:
$Cu^{2+}/Cu = +0.34$ V, $Ni^{2+}/Ni = -0.25$ V, $Zn^{2+}/Zn = -0.76$ V, $Al^{3+}/Al = -1.66$ V, $Mg^{2+}/Mg = -2.36$ V.
Which option arranges these metals in increasing order of reducing power?
options: Mg < Al < Zn < Ni < Cu
Cu < Zn < Ni < Al < Mg
Cu < Ni < Zn < Al < Mg
Ni < Cu < Zn < Mg < Al
questions.explanation:
Reducing power rises as $E^\circ$ becomes more negative.
Ordering from most positive to most negative: Cu (+0.34) > Ni (−0.25) > Zn (−0.76) > Al (−1.66) > Mg (−2.36).
So the increasing order of reducing power is Cu < Ni < Zn < Al < Mg.
Option (1) is the reverse order. Option (2) wrongly swaps Ni and Zn.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Hydrazine reacts with chlorate ion in basic medium to give nitric oxide and chloride ion: $\mathrm{N_2H_4 + ClO_3^- \rightarrow NO + Cl^-}$. Consider the following statements about the reaction balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients.
(i) $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$ is the oxidising agent.
(ii) Each $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ molecule loses 8 electrons.
(iii) $\mathrm{OH^-}$ ions must appear in the final balanced equation.
(iv) $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ and $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$ react in the mole ratio 3 : 4.
(v) Six water molecules appear on the product side.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Cl changes from +5 to –1, a gain of 6 electrons. N changes from –2 to +2, so 2 N atoms lose 8 electrons per $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$. The LCM of 6 and 8 is 24, giving 3 $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ and 4 $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$.
Balanced equation: $\mathrm{3N_2H_4 + 4ClO_3^- \rightarrow 6NO + 4Cl^- + 6H_2O}$. Charge (–4) and H (12) already balance, so no $\mathrm{OH^-}$ is needed.
(i) correct, (ii) correct, (iii) incorrect, (iv) correct, (v) correct.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Excess chlorine in drinking water is removed by passing sulphur dioxide: $Cl_2 + SO_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2Cl^- + SO_4^{2-} + 4H^+$.
Assertion (A): $SO_2$ acts as the reducing agent in this reaction.
Reason (R): The oxidation number of sulphur increases from +4 to +6, while that of chlorine decreases from 0 to −1.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: S goes from +4 in $SO_2$ to +6 in $SO_4^{2-}$, and Cl goes from 0 to −1.
A is true: $SO_2$ is oxidised and so lowers the oxidation number of chlorine. A reagent that lowers another element's oxidation number is the reducing agent.
R directly explains A, since the increase in sulphur's oxidation number is what makes $SO_2$ the reductant.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calcium hydride, $CaH_2$, is an ionic compound that can be written as $Ca^{2+}(H^-)_2$. For its formation from Ca(s) and $H_2(g)$, which option correctly gives the oxidation half, the reduction half and the moles of electrons transferred per mole of $CaH_2$?
options: Oxidation: $H_2 \rightarrow 2H^+ + 2e^-$; Reduction: $Ca^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Ca$; 2 mol
Oxidation: $Ca \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2e^-$; Reduction: $H_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2H^-$; 4 mol
Oxidation: $Ca \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2e^-$; Reduction: $2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2$; 2 mol
Oxidation: $Ca \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2e^-$; Reduction: $H_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2H^-$; 2 mol
questions.explanation:
Ca ends up as $Ca^{2+}$, so it loses 2 electrons: $Ca \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2e^-$ (oxidation).
H ends up as $H^-$, so each $H_2$ gains 2 electrons: $H_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2H^-$ (reduction).
One mole of $CaH_2$ therefore involves 2 mol of electrons, not 4, which double-counts.
Option (3) wrongly treats hydrogen as $H^+$, as it would be in an acid.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
A 25.0 mL sample of a Cu$^{2+}$ solution is treated with excess KI. The iodine liberated requires 20.0 mL of 0.100 M Na$_2$S$_2$O$_3$ for complete reaction, using starch as indicator.
Reactions: 2Cu$^{2+}$ + 4I$^-$ → Cu$_2$I$_2$ + I$_2$; I$_2$ + 2S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ → 2I$^-$ + S$_4$O$_6^{2-}$.
What is the molarity of Cu$^{2+}$ in the sample?
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Permanganate ion oxidises bromide ion in basic medium to bromate ion and is itself converted to $MnO_2$. In the balanced ionic equation, what is the mole ratio $MnO_4^- : Br^-$?
questions.explanation:
Mn goes from +7 to +4, a decrease of 3. Br goes from −1 to +5, an increase of 6.
Equating the changes requires 2 $MnO_4^-$ for every 1 $Br^-$.
The balanced equation is $2MnO_4^- + Br^- + H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + BrO_3^- + 2OH^-$.
So the ratio is 2 : 1.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: In $HCHO + 2Cu^{2+} + 5OH^- \rightarrow Cu_2O + HCOO^- + 3H_2O$, the oxidation number of carbon rises from 0 to $+2$ while that of copper falls from $+2$ to $+1$
$AgF_2$, if formed, behaves as a very strong oxidant because silver in it is in the unusual $+2$ state and readily accepts an electron to reach $+1$
When carbon burns in excess dioxygen, $CO_2$ (C: $+4$) is formed, whereas with limited dioxygen $CO$ (C: $+2$) is formed
In $H_2O(s) + F_2(g) \rightarrow HF + HOF$, fluorine undergoes disproportionation, since it is $-1$ in HF and $+1$ in HOF
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: C in HCHO is 0 and in $HCOO^-$ is $+2$. Cu goes from $+2$ to $+1$ in $Cu_2O$.
(2) Correct: Ag(II) is unstable. Its strong tendency to gain an electron and become Ag(I) makes $AgF_2$ a powerful oxidant.
(3) Correct: excess oxidant gives the higher oxidation state of carbon, limited oxidant gives the lower one.
(4) Incorrect: fluorine, the most electronegative element, cannot show a positive oxidation number. In HOF, F is $-1$, H is $+1$ and O is 0. Fluorine is reduced in both products and oxygen is oxidised from $-2$ to 0.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the thermite-type reaction $Cr_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow Al_2O_3(s) + 2Cr(s)$, which statement is INCORRECT?
options: Aluminium acts as the reducing agent
Oxidation number of each Cr atom decreases by 3
Oxygen is oxidised as its oxidation number changes during the reaction
Aluminium is a better reducing agent than chromium
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Al goes from 0 to +3. It is oxidised, so it acts as the reductant.
(2) Correct: Cr goes from +3 to 0, a decrease of 3 per atom.
(3) Incorrect: oxygen is –2 in both $Cr_2O_3$ and $Al_2O_3$, so its oxidation number does not change.
(4) Correct: in metal displacement, the displacing metal loses electrons more readily than the metal it displaces.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the layer test, chlorine water is added to an aqueous KI solution and the mixture is shaken with $CCl_4$. The $CCl_4$ layer becomes coloured. Which species is responsible for this colour?
questions.explanation:
Cl2 is a stronger oxidant than I2. It oxidises iodide ions: $Cl_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + I_2$.
The I2 formed is coloured and dissolves in CCl4, so it colours the organic layer.
I– and K+ are colourless ions that stay in water. Cl2 is consumed in the reaction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In $CrO_5$, the oxidation number of chromium is $+6$, not $+10$.
Reason (R): $CrO_5$ contains one oxygen at $-2$ and four oxygen atoms in peroxide linkages, each at $-1$.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
If all five O atoms were taken as −2, Cr would come out as +10. That is impossible, because group 6 elements cannot exceed +6.
R is true: $CrO_5$ has four peroxide oxygens (−1 each) and one oxo oxygen (−2).
Sum rule: $x + 4(-1) + (-2) = 0$, so $x = +6$. A is true.
R is exactly why A holds.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Permanganate ion oxidises oxalate ion in acidic medium:
$MnO_4^- + C_2O_4^{2-} + H^+ \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + CO_2 + H_2O$ (unbalanced)
After balancing with the smallest whole-number coefficients, how many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The coefficient of $H^+$ is 16.
(ii) The total number of electrons transferred is 10.
(iii) The mole ratio $MnO_4^- : C_2O_4^{2-}$ is 5 : 2.
(iv) The oxidation number of carbon changes from +3 to +4.
(v) The coefficient of $H_2O$ is 8.
questions.explanation:
Reduction half: Mn goes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 e⁻ per $MnO_4^-$.
Oxidation half: C goes from +3 to +4, so each $C_2O_4^{2-}$ loses 2 e⁻.
Equalising electrons gives $2MnO_4^- + 5C_2O_4^{2-} + 16H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 10CO_2 + 8H_2O$, with 10 e⁻ transferred.
Check: charge is +4 on both sides; O is 28 on both sides.
Statements (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are correct. Statement (iii) is wrong because the ratio is 2 : 5.
Total correct = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chlorine, bromine and iodine disproportionate in alkaline solution, but fluorine does not.
Reason (R): Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, cannot exhibit any positive oxidation state.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $Cl_2$ in alkali gives $Cl^-$ (−1) and $ClO^-$ (+1), and $Br_2$ and $I_2$ behave in the same way. With alkali, $F_2$ instead gives $F^-$ and $OF_2$.
R is true. F is the most electronegative element, so it shows only $0$ and $-1$.
For disproportionation, the element must be able to go to a higher and a lower state. F cannot go above zero, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A half reaction for a change in basic medium is being balanced by the ion-electron method. O atoms have been balanced with $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and H atoms with $\mathrm{H^+}$. What is the correct next step to convert it to basic medium?
options: Replace every $\mathrm{H^+}$ by $\mathrm{OH^-}$ on the same side
Add as many $\mathrm{OH^-}$ ions to both sides as there are $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions, then combine $\mathrm{H^+}$ and $\mathrm{OH^-}$ on the same side into $\mathrm{H_2O}$
Add $\mathrm{OH^-}$ ions only to the side opposite to $\mathrm{H^+}$
Remove all $\mathrm{H^+}$ and balance the charge using electrons alone
questions.explanation:
NCERT rule: for each $\mathrm{H^+}$, add an equal number of $\mathrm{OH^-}$ to both sides of the equation. This keeps the equation balanced.
Where $\mathrm{H^+}$ and $\mathrm{OH^-}$ appear together, they combine to give $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
Example: $\mathrm{MnO_4^- + 4H^+ \rightarrow MnO_2 + 2H_2O}$ becomes $\mathrm{MnO_4^- + 2H_2O \rightarrow MnO_2 + 4OH^-}$.
Simply swapping $\mathrm{H^+}$ for $\mathrm{OH^-}$ (option 1) destroys both the atom and charge balance.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A strip of metallic zinc is kept in an aqueous solution of copper nitrate for about one hour. Which pair of observations is expected?
options: The strip gets a reddish coating and the blue colour of the solution fades
The strip gets a silvery coating and the solution turns blue
The strip dissolves completely and the solution turns green
No visible change occurs because zinc cannot reduce $Cu^{2+}$
questions.explanation:
Zinc loses electrons and goes into solution as $Zn^{2+}$: $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) \to Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$.
The $Cu^{2+}$ ions gain these electrons and deposit as reddish metallic copper on the strip.
The blue colour of the solution comes from $Cu^{2+}$, so it fades as these ions are used up.
Option (4) is wrong because zinc releases electrons more readily than copper.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The average oxidation number of lead in $Pb_3O_4$ is $+\frac{8}{3}$.
Statement II: $Pb_3O_4$ contains lead in the $+2$ and $+4$ states in the ratio Pb(II) : Pb(IV) = 1 : 2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I: $3x + 4(-2) = 0$, so $x = +\frac{8}{3}$. True.
A fractional value is only an average. NCERT treats $Pb_3O_4$ as a mixed oxide, $2PbO \cdot PbO_2$.
That means 2 Pb(II) and 1 Pb(IV), a 2 : 1 ratio. Check: $(2 \times 2 + 4)/3 = \frac{8}{3}$.
Statement II gives the ratio reversed, so it is false.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to its structure, what are the actual oxidation states of the three carbon atoms in carbon suboxide, $C_3O_2$ (O=C=C=C=O), from one end to the other?
questions.explanation:
Rule-based calculation gives an average of $\frac{4}{3}$ per carbon: $3x + 2(-2) = 0$.
The structure O=C=C=C=O shows that each terminal carbon is bonded to an oxygen, so each is +2.
The central carbon is bonded only to carbon atoms, so it is 0.
The average $\frac{2+0+2}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$ is not the real state of any single atom, so option (1) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In the reaction $Pb_3O_4 + 8HCl \rightarrow 3PbCl_2 + Cl_2 + 4H_2O$, only one of the three lead atoms of $Pb_3O_4$ undergoes reduction.
Statement II: The reaction $Pb_3O_4 + 4HNO_3 \rightarrow 2Pb(NO_3)_2 + PbO_2 + 2H_2O$ is not a redox reaction.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
$Pb_3O_4$ behaves as 2PbO·$PbO_2$, containing two Pb(II) and one Pb(IV).
Statement I is correct. With HCl, the 2PbO part undergoes only an acid–base reaction. Only the Pb(IV) of $PbO_2$ is reduced to +2, while it oxidises $Cl^-$ to $Cl_2$.
Statement II is correct. With $HNO_3$, only PbO reacts (acid–base), and $PbO_2$ remains unchanged because it is passive towards the oxidising acid. Pb stays +2 and +4, and N stays +5.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Peroxomonosulphuric acid, $H_2SO_5$, contains one O–O linkage. If every oxygen is wrongly taken as $-2$, the oxidation number of sulphur comes out as $+8$. Which option gives the correct oxidation number of sulphur and the correct reasoning?
options: $+8$, since the sum rule must always be obeyed with oxygen as $-2$
$+6$, since two oxygens form a peroxide linkage ($-1$ each) and the other three are $-2$
$+7$, since one oxygen is in the superoxide state
$+6$, since hydrogen is $-1$ in this compound
questions.explanation:
Sulphur is in group 16, so its maximum oxidation number is 16 − 10 = +6. A value of +8 is impossible.
The two peroxide oxygens are each $-1$, the remaining three oxygens are $-2$, and H is +1.
The sum is 2(+1) + x + 3(−2) + 2(−1) = 0, so x = +6.
Option (4) reaches +6 by wrong reasoning: H is bonded to O, so it is +1, not $-1$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the electrolysis set-ups in List-I with the products in List-II.
List-I
(A) Aqueous $AgNO_3$ with silver electrodes
(B) Aqueous $AgNO_3$ with platinum electrodes
(C) Dilute $H_2SO_4$ with platinum electrodes
(D) Aqueous $CuCl_2$ with platinum electrodes
List-II
(P) $H_2$ at cathode, $O_2$ at anode
(Q) Cu at cathode, $Cl_2$ at anode
(R) Ag deposited at cathode, silver anode dissolves as $Ag^+$
(S) Ag deposited at cathode, $O_2$ at anode
options: A-S, B-R, C-P, D-Q
A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q
A-R, B-S, C-Q, D-P
A-P, B-S, C-R, D-Q
questions.explanation:
(A) Ag⁺ is reduced at the cathode. The silver anode is itself oxidised to Ag⁺ more easily than water is, so the anode dissolves: R.
(B) The Pt anode is inert, so water is oxidised to $O_2$, while Ag deposits at the cathode: S.
(C) $H^+$ is reduced to $H_2$ and water is oxidised to $O_2$: P.
(D) Cu²⁺ is reduced to Cu, and Cl⁻ is oxidised to $Cl_2$: Q.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the species in List-I with the oxidation number of the stated element in List-II.
List-I
(A) N in $NH_4^+$
(B) Cr in $K_2CrO_4$
(C) P in $H_3PO_3$
(D) Cl in $KClO_3$
List-II
(i) $+3$
(ii) $-3$
(iii) $+5$
(iv) $+6$
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(i)
