questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction).
List-I:
(a) $N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2NO(g)$
(b) $2KClO_3(s) \rightarrow 2KCl(s) + 3O_2(g)$
(c) $Zn(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)$
(d) $Cl_2(g) + 2OH^-(aq) \rightarrow ClO^-(aq) + Cl^-(aq) + H_2O(l)$
List-II:
(i) Disproportionation
(ii) Combination
(iii) Displacement
(iv) Decomposition
questions.explanation:
(a) Two elements combine to form NO, so it is a combination reaction (ii).
(b) One compound breaks into KCl and elemental $O_2$, so it is a decomposition reaction (iv).
(c) Zn displaces Cu from its salt, so it is a metal displacement reaction (iii).
(d) Cl in $Cl_2$ (0) goes to both +1 in $ClO^-$ and −1 in $Cl^-$, so it is disproportionation (i).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Permanganate ion oxidises sulphur dioxide in acidic solution: $\mathrm{MnO_4^- + SO_2 \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + HSO_4^-}$. When the equation is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, which statement about it is correct?
options: 4 $\mathrm{H^+}$ appear on the product side
2 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and 1 $\mathrm{H^+}$ appear on the reactant side
2 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ appear on the product side and no $\mathrm{H^+}$ is needed
The mole ratio $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ : $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is 5 : 2
questions.explanation:
Oxidation half: $\mathrm{SO_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow HSO_4^- + 3H^+ + 2e^-}$, multiplied by 5.
Reduction half: $\mathrm{MnO_4^- + 8H^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O}$, multiplied by 2.
Adding: on the H⁺ side, 16 on the left and 15 on the right leave a net 1 $\mathrm{H^+}$ on the left. For water, 10 on the left and 8 on the right leave a net 2 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ on the left.
Balanced equation: $\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + 5SO_2 + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 5HSO_4^-}$. Charge is –1 on each side.
The ratio $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ : $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is 2 : 5, not 5 : 2.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the earliest (limited) meaning of oxidation, which of the following is an example of oxidation of an element by addition of oxygen?
options: $2Mg(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2MgO(s)$
$2HgO(s) \rightarrow 2Hg(l) + O_2(g)$
$CH_2=CH_2(g) + H_2(g) \rightarrow H_3C-CH_3(g)$
$2FeCl_3(aq) + H_2(g) \rightarrow 2FeCl_2(aq) + 2HCl(aq)$
questions.explanation:
Originally, oxidation meant addition of oxygen to an element or compound.
In $2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO$, oxygen is added to the element magnesium, so Mg is oxidised.
HgO loses oxygen, so it is reduced, not oxidised.
Ethene gains hydrogen and FeCl3 loses chlorine; both are reductions.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the effect of excess oxidant or excess reductant are correct?
(i) Carbon burnt in a limited supply of $O_2$ gives CO, but in excess $O_2$ gives $CO_2$.
(ii) $P_4$ reacting with excess $Cl_2$ gives $PCl_3$ as the main product.
(iii) Sodium burnt in excess $O_2$ gives $Na_2O_2$, in which oxygen has a higher oxidation number than in $Na_2O$.
(iv) In general, the product with the higher oxidation state forms when the reducing agent is in excess.
questions.explanation:
General rule: excess oxidant gives the product with the higher oxidation state; excess reductant gives the lower one.
(i) Correct: C reaches +2 in CO and +4 in $CO_2$ (excess $O_2$).
(ii) Incorrect: Excess $Cl_2$ (oxidant) gives $PCl_5$ (P +5). $PCl_3$ forms when $P_4$ is in excess.
(iii) Correct: O is −1 in $Na_2O_2$, compared with −2 in $Na_2O$. This is the higher oxidation state with excess oxidant.
(iv) Incorrect: This reverses the rule.
Two statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (species) with List-II (real oxidation states of the indicated element, as revealed by structure):
List-I
(A) $C_3O_2$ (C)
(B) $Br_3O_8$ (Br)
(C) $S_4O_6^{2-}$ (S)
(D) $Fe_3O_4$ (Fe)
List-II
(I) +6, +4, +6
(II) +2, +3, +3
(III) +2, 0, +2
(IV) +5, 0, 0, +5
options: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
(A) $C_3O_2$: the terminal carbons are +2 and the middle carbon is 0, so A matches III.
(B) $Br_3O_8$: the terminal bromines are +6 and the middle bromine is +4 (average 16/3), so B matches I.
(C) $S_4O_6^{2-}$: the end sulphurs are +5 and the middle two are 0, so C matches IV.
(D) $Fe_3O_4$ = FeO·$Fe_2O_3$: one Fe is +2 and two are +3 (average 8/3), so D matches II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction):
List-I
(a) $3Mg + N_2 \rightarrow Mg_3N_2$
(b) $2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$
(c) $V_2O_5 + 5Ca \rightarrow 2V + 5CaO$
(d) $2Na + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH + H_2$
List-II
(i) Metal displacement
(ii) Non-metal displacement
(iii) Combination
(iv) Decomposition
questions.explanation:
(a) Two elements combine to form $Mg_3N_2$, so this is combination: (iii).
(b) One compound breaks into KCl and elemental $O_2$, so this is decomposition: (iv).
(c) Ca displaces the metal V from its oxide, so this is metal displacement: (i).
(d) Na displaces the non-metal hydrogen from water, so this is non-metal displacement: (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $2HgCl_2(aq) + SnCl_2(aq) \rightarrow Hg_2Cl_2(s) + SnCl_4(aq)$, the oxidation numbers of Hg and Sn change respectively as:
options: +2 to 0 and +2 to +4
+1 to +2 and +4 to +2
+2 to +1 and +4 to +2
+2 to +1 and +2 to +4
questions.explanation:
Hg in $HgCl_2$ is +2. In $Hg_2Cl_2$ it is +1, so mercury is reduced. Hg$_2$(I)Cl$_2$ is the reduced form of Hg(II)Cl$_2$.
Sn in $SnCl_2$ is +2. In $SnCl_4$ it is +4, so tin is oxidised.
Option (1) is wrong because mercury does not reach the metal (0) in this reaction.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A Daniell cell is set up. A zinc rod dips in zinc sulphate solution and a copper rod dips in copper sulphate solution. The two solutions are joined by a salt bridge, and the rods are connected through a wire with an ammeter. When the switch is closed, which statement is correct?
options: Electrons move from the zinc rod to the copper rod through the salt bridge
Conventional current flows from the zinc rod to the copper rod in the external wire
Zinc is oxidised at the zinc rod, which acts as the anode
$Cu^{2+}$ ions are reduced at the anode
questions.explanation:
Zinc loses electrons and forms $Zn^{2+}$, so oxidation occurs at the zinc rod. The electrode where oxidation occurs is the anode.
Electrons travel through the metallic wire, not through the salt bridge. The salt bridge carries charge by the migration of ions.
Current flows opposite to electron flow, so in the wire it flows from Cu to Zn.
$Cu^{2+}$ is reduced at the cathode, not the anode.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following does oxygen have a positive oxidation number?
questions.explanation:
Fluorine is always −1, so in $O_2F_2$: $2x + 2(-1) = 0$, giving $x = +1$.
In $H_2O_2$ and $Na_2O_2$ (peroxides), oxygen is −1.
In $KO_2$ (a superoxide), oxygen is $-\frac{1}{2}$.
Oxygen becomes positive only when it is bonded to fluorine, which is more electronegative than oxygen.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In sodium borohydride, $NaBH_4$, boron has an oxidation number of $+3$.
Statement II: In $NaBH_4$, each hydrogen has an oxidation number of $+1$ because it is attached to the non-metal boron.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
In $NaBH_4$, hydrogen carries a hydride-like charge, so H = $-1$. Na, an alkali metal, is +1.
Statement I: +1 + x + 4(−1) = 0, so x = +3. This is correct.
Statement II: If H were +1, the sum would give B = −5, which is not the accepted value. H is $-1$ here, so the statement is incorrect.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation number of each oxygen atom in potassium superoxide, $KO_2$, is:
questions.explanation:
K is an alkali metal, so it is +1.
The sum of oxidation numbers is zero: +1 + 2x = 0, so x = $-\frac{1}{2}$.
In superoxides the two O atoms are directly linked to each other, and each O is assigned $-\frac{1}{2}$.
The value $-1$ applies to peroxides such as $Na_2O_2$, not to superoxides.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following species can undergo disproportionation?
$ClO^-$, $ClO_4^-$, $H_2O_2$, $F_2$, $NO_2$, $Mn^{3+}$, $Cl_2$ (in alkali), $MnO_4^-$
questions.explanation:
$ClO^-$ (Cl +1): yes.
$H_2O_2$ (O $-1$): yes, gives $H_2O$ and $O_2$.
$NO_2$ (N +4): yes, gives $NO_2^-$ and $NO_3^-$.
$Mn^{3+}$: yes, gives $Mn^{2+}$ and $MnO_2$.
$Cl_2$ in alkali: yes, gives $Cl^-$ and $ClO^-$.
$ClO_4^-$ (Cl +7) and $MnO_4^-$ (Mn +7): no, both are in the highest oxidation state.
$F_2$: no, fluorine cannot show a positive oxidation state.
Total = 5.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: $Hg_2Cl_2$ represents the reduced form of $HgCl_2$, as shown by the Stock notations Hg(I) and Hg(II)
In $Br_3O_8$, each of the three bromine atoms is actually present in the +16/3 oxidation state
In $HAuCl_4$, gold is in the +3 oxidation state and the compound can be written as $HAu(III)Cl_4$
The average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion $S_4O_6^{2-}$ is +2.5
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Hg goes from +2 in $HgCl_2$ to +1 in $Hg_2Cl_2$, so $Hg_2Cl_2$ is the reduced form.
(2) Incorrect: +16/3 is only an average. From the structure, the two terminal Br atoms are +6 and the middle Br is +4.
(3) Correct: 1 + x – 4 = 0 gives x = +3.
(4) Correct: 4x – 12 = –2 gives x = 2.5.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In acidic medium, permanganate oxidises oxalate ion to $CO_2$ and is itself reduced to $Mn^{2+}$. What volume of 0.02 M $KMnO_4$ is needed to completely oxidise 25 mL of 0.1 M sodium oxalate solution?
options: 20 mL
50 mL
100 mL
125 mL
questions.explanation:
Given: oxalate = 25 mL of 0.1 M, so moles = $2.5\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Balanced equation: Mn goes from +7 to +2 (gains 5e⁻), and each $C_2O_4^{2-}$ loses 2e⁻. This gives $2MnO_4^- + 5C_2O_4^{2-} + 16H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 10CO_2 + 8H_2O$.
Moles of $MnO_4^-$ = $\frac{2}{5}\times2.5\times10^{-3} = 1.0\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Volume = $1.0\times10^{-3}/0.02$ = 0.05 L = 50 mL.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about halogen displacement reactions is INCORRECT?
options: Chlorine can displace both bromide and iodide ions from their aqueous solutions
Bromine can oxidise iodide ions to iodine in solution
Displacement of chloride and bromide ions by fluorine is usually carried out in aqueous solution because fluorine is the most reactive halogen
In the reaction $2F_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 4HF + O_2$, the oxidation number of oxygen increases from –2 to 0
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Cl2 oxidises both Br– and I–. This is the basis of the layer test.
(2) Correct: $Br_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Br^- + I_2$.
(3) Incorrect: F2 is so reactive that it attacks water itself and releases O2. For this reason, its displacement reactions are generally NOT carried out in aqueous solution.
(4) Correct: O goes from –2 in H2O to 0 in O2, while F goes from 0 to –1.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (titration system) with List-II (observation):
List-I
(a) MnO$_4^-$ titrated against C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ in acid
(b) Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ titrated against Fe$^{2+}$
(c) Liberated I$_2$ titrated with S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ using starch
(d) Cu$^{2+}$ treated with excess I$^-$
List-II
(i) Indicator oxidised just after the equivalence point to give intense blue
(ii) First lasting pink tinge marks the end point
(iii) Blue colour vanishes at the end point
(iv) A precipitate forms along with free iodine
options: a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv
a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
questions.explanation:
(a)-(ii): permanganate is a self-indicator; its first lasting pink tinge marks the end point.
(b)-(i): dichromate oxidises diphenylamine just after the equivalence point, giving blue.
(c)-(iii): the starch–iodine blue disappears when all the I$_2$ has reacted with thiosulphate.
(d)-(iv): Cu$^{2+}$ with excess I$^-$ gives a Cu$_2$I$_2$ precipitate and I$_2$.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given standard reduction potentials at 298 K:
$MnO_4^-/Mn^{2+}$ (acidic) = +1.51 V, $Cl_2/Cl^-$ = +1.36 V, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}/Cr^{3+}$ (acidic) = +1.33 V, $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}$ = +0.77 V.
Statement I: Under standard conditions, $Cl_2$ can oxidise $Mn^{2+}$ to $MnO_4^-$ in acidic solution.
Statement II: Under standard conditions, acidified $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ can oxidise $Fe^{2+}$ to $Fe^{3+}$.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
A species can oxidise another if its couple has the higher (more positive) reduction potential.
Statement I is incorrect. $MnO_4^-$ (1.51 V) is a stronger oxidant than $Cl_2$ (1.36 V), so $Cl_2$ cannot convert $Mn^{2+}$ into $MnO_4^-$.
Statement II is correct. 1.33 V > 0.77 V, so dichromate oxidises $Fe^{2+}$. This is the basis of dichromate titrations.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion, $S_4O_6^{2-}$, is 2.5. According to its structure, the actual oxidation states of the four sulphur atoms (two terminal and two middle) are:
options: +2.5 on each sulphur atom
questions.explanation:
A fractional oxidation number is only an average. The structure shows the real oxidation states.
In $S_4O_6^{2-}$, the two terminal S atoms are bonded to oxygen and are +5 each.
The two middle S atoms are bonded only to sulphur and are 0 each.
Check: (5 + 0 + 0 + 5)/4 = 2.5.
Option (1) is wrong because electrons are never transferred in fractions.
Option (3) also averages 2.5, but it does not match the structure.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction $2H_2S(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2S(s) + 2H_2O(l)$, hydrogen sulphide is regarded as oxidised in the classical sense mainly because:
options: oxygen is added to sulphur
hydrogen is removed from it
an electropositive element is added to it
sulphur gains hydrogen
questions.explanation:
H2S changes to S, so the hydrogen attached to sulphur is removed.
The classical definition was broadened to include removal of hydrogen as oxidation.
No oxygen ends up on sulphur here, because sulphur appears as the free element, so option (1) fails.
Adding an electropositive element would mean reduction, not oxidation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Excess chlorine in drinking water is removed by passing sulphur dioxide, which gives chloride and sulphate ions in solution.
Statement I: In this change, each $\mathrm{SO_2}$ molecule loses 2 electrons, and $\mathrm{SO_2}$ acts as the reducing agent.
Statement II: In the balanced equation, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ react in the mole ratio 1 : 1.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Balanced equation: $\mathrm{Cl_2 + SO_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2Cl^- + SO_4^{2-} + 4H^+}$.
Statement I is correct: S changes from +4 to +6, so it loses 2 electrons and $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is the reductant. Cl changes from 0 to –1, so 2 Cl atoms gain the 2 electrons.
Statement II is incorrect: 2 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ are needed to supply the oxygen for sulphate, so the ratio $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ : $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is 1 : 2.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The average oxidation number of carbon in acetic acid, $CH_3COOH$, is zero. However, the two carbon atoms are not in the same state. The actual oxidation numbers of the methyl carbon and the carboxyl carbon are, respectively:
options: 0 and 0
questions.explanation:
Average from the formula $C_2H_4O_2$: 2x + 4(+1) + 2(−2) = 0, so x = 0.
In the bonding picture, the bond pair goes to the more electronegative atom, and a C–C bond contributes nothing.
Methyl carbon: it has three C–H bonds, each giving −1, so it is $-3$.
Carboxyl carbon: the C=O bond gives +2 and the C–OH bond gives +1, so it is $+3$.
The average, (−3 + 3)/2 = 0, hides this difference. This is similar to the fractional cases such as $Fe_3O_4$.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When hydrogen peroxide decomposes as $2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$, the oxygen atoms present in $H_2O_2$ end up in which oxidation states?
options: $-2$ in $H_2O$ and $0$ in $O_2$
$-1$ in $H_2O$ and $0$ in $O_2$
$-2$ in both $H_2O$ and $O_2$
questions.explanation:
In the peroxide $H_2O_2$, each O atom has oxidation number $-1$.
In $H_2O$, O is $-2$, so these O atoms are reduced.
In free $O_2$, O is $0$, so these O atoms are oxidised.
The same element in one intermediate state goes to a higher and a lower state at the same time, so this is a disproportionation.
Option (2) fails because O in $H_2O$ is $-2$, not $-1$.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are disproportionation reactions?
(i) $2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$
(ii) $Cl_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow ClO^- + Cl^- + H_2O$
(iii) $2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$
(iv) $2NO_2 + 2OH^- \rightarrow NO_2^- + NO_3^- + H_2O$
(v) $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$
(vi) $P_4 + 3OH^- + 3H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_2PO_2^-$
questions.explanation:
(i) Yes: O goes from –1 to –2 and 0.
(ii) Yes: Cl goes from 0 to +1 and –1.
(iii) No: Cl is reduced (+5 to –1) while O is oxidised (–2 to 0). These are different elements, so it is a decomposition redox reaction.
(iv) Yes: N goes from +4 to +3 and +5.
(v) No: no oxidation number changes, so it is not redox at all.
(vi) Yes: P goes from 0 to –3 and +1.
Total = 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about oxidation numbers is INCORRECT?
options: In $CaO_2$, calcium is $+2$ and each oxygen is $-1$
In hypochlorous acid, $HOCl$, chlorine has an oxidation number of $+1$
In $HClO_4$, chlorine shows its highest oxidation number, $+7$
In $ClF_3$, chlorine has an oxidation number of $-1$ because halogens are always $-1$
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Ca is an alkaline earth metal (+2). $CaO_2$ is a peroxide, so each O is $-1$.
(2) Correct: +1 + x − 2 = 0, so Cl = +1.
(3) Correct: +1 + x − 8 = 0, so Cl = +7, which equals 17 − 10.
(4) Incorrect: only fluorine is always $-1$. Cl, Br and I are $-1$ only as halide ions. In $ClF_3$, x + 3(−1) = 0, so Cl = +3.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (redox reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction).
List-I
(A) $N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2NO(g)$
(B) $2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)$
(C) $NaH(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow NaOH(aq) + H_2(g)$
(D) $2NO_2(g) + 2OH^-(aq) \rightarrow NO_2^-(aq) + NO_3^-(aq) + H_2O(l)$
List-II
(I) Displacement
(II) Disproportionation
(III) Combination
(IV) Decomposition
options: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
questions.explanation:
(A) Two elements combine to form NO, so it is a combination reaction: III.
(B) Lead nitrate breaks down into three components, so it is a decomposition reaction: IV.
(C) The hydride ion displaces hydrogen of water as $H_2$, so it is a displacement reaction: I.
(D) N in $NO_2$ (+4) goes to $NO_2^-$ (+3) and $NO_3^-$ (+5), so it is a disproportionation reaction: II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
A strip of each metal is dipped in the aqueous salt solution indicated. In how many cases will the metal displace the metal ion from solution?
(i) Zn in $FeSO_4$
(ii) Fe in $ZnSO_4$
(iii) Al in $CuSO_4$
(iv) Cu in $MgSO_4$
(v) Mg in $FeSO_4$
(vi) Fe in $CuSO_4$
(vii) Zn in $Al_2(SO_4)_3$
questions.explanation:
The order of displacement (reducing power) is Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu. A metal displaces only a metal that lies after it in this order.
(i) Zn > Fe, so it reacts. (ii) Fe < Zn, so there is no reaction.
(iii) Al > Cu, so it reacts. (iv) Cu < Mg, so there is no reaction.
(v) Mg > Fe, so it reacts. (vi) Fe > Cu, so it reacts.
(vii) Zn < Al, so there is no reaction.
The total number of reacting cases is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are redox reactions?
(i) $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$
(ii) $2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$
(iii) $NaH + H_2O \rightarrow NaOH + H_2$
(iv) $2PbO + 4HCl \rightarrow 2PbCl_2 + 2H_2O$
(v) $N_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2NO$
(vi) $AgNO_3 + NaCl \rightarrow AgCl + NaNO_3$
(vii) $Cl_2 + 2KI \rightarrow 2KCl + I_2$
questions.explanation:
(i) Not redox: Ca stays +2, C stays +4, O stays −2.
(ii) Redox: oxygen at −1 goes to 0 and −2 (disproportionation).
(iii) Redox: hydride H (−1) and water H (+1) both become 0 in $H_2$.
(iv) Not redox: this is an acid–base reaction; Pb stays +2.
(v) Redox: N goes 0 → +2 and O goes 0 → −2.
(vi) Not redox: this is a precipitation reaction.
(vii) Redox: $I^-$ is oxidised and $Cl_2$ is reduced.
Total redox reactions = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the titration of an acidified Fe$^{2+}$ solution against KMnO$_4$, no separate indicator is added. Why?
options: Fe$^{3+}$ formed in the reaction gives a deep blue colour at the end point
Mn$^{2+}$ formed in the reaction is intensely purple
MnO$_4^-$ is intensely coloured, so the first lasting pink tinge after the last Fe$^{2+}$ is oxidised marks the end point
Fe$^{2+}$ forms a red complex with excess MnO$_4^-$ only at the equivalence point
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: permanganate is itself intensely coloured, so it acts as a self-indicator.
While Fe$^{2+}$ remains, each drop of MnO$_4^-$ is reduced and its colour vanishes.
Once the last Fe$^{2+}$ is oxidised, the next drop leaves a lasting pink tinge. This is the end point, with very little overshoot.
Option (2) is tempting but wrong: Mn$^{2+}$ is nearly colourless. The colour comes from unreacted MnO$_4^-$.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the more recent view mentioned in NCERT, which describes the limitation of the oxidation-number concept, oxidation is visualised as:
options: an increase in electron density around the atom(s) involved
a decrease in electron density around the atom(s) involved
complete transfer of electrons from the more electronegative atom to the less electronegative atom
addition of hydrogen to a substance
questions.explanation:
The concept of redox has kept evolving over time.
In the recent view, oxidation is a decrease in electron density around the atom(s), and reduction is an increase.
Option (1) describes reduction, not oxidation.
Option (3) reverses the book-keeping assumption: electrons are assumed to move to the more electronegative atom.
Option (4) is a classical definition of reduction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion, $S_4O_6^{2-}$, is +2.5.
Statement II: In carbon suboxide, $C_3O_2$, the central carbon is in the +2 state and each terminal carbon is in the zero state.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I: 4x + 6(–2) = –2, so x = +2.5. This is correct. It is only an average; the structure shows the sulphurs as +5, 0, 0 and +5.
Statement II: In O=C=C=C=O, each terminal carbon is bonded to oxygen and is +2. The central carbon is 0. Statement II reverses this, so it is incorrect.
Check: the average is (2 + 0 + 2)/3 = 4/3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Fluorine reacts with ice: $H_2O(s) + F_2(g) \rightarrow HF(g) + HOF(g)$
Statement I: The oxidation number of oxygen in HOF is zero.
Statement II: In this reaction fluorine undergoes both oxidation and reduction.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I: In HOF, H is +1 and F is −1 (F is always −1 in compounds). So O = 0. Correct.
Statement II: Both F atoms go from 0 in $F_2$ to −1 (one in HF, one in HOF). Fluorine is only reduced. Oxygen (−2 to 0) is the species oxidised. Incorrect.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Formaldehyde reacts with Tollens' and Fehling's reagents as follows:
$HCHO + 2[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+ + 3OH^- \rightarrow 2Ag + HCOO^- + 4NH_3 + 2H_2O$
$HCHO + 2Cu^{2+} + 5OH^- \rightarrow Cu_2O + HCOO^- + 3H_2O$
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Carbon changes from 0 in HCHO to +2 in $HCOO^-$ in both reactions
In each reaction, two moles of electrons are transferred per mole of HCHO
In the reaction with Fehling's reagent, copper is reduced from +2 to 0
Neither $NH_3$ nor $OH^-$ undergoes a change in oxidation number
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: In HCHO, C = 0 (2×(+1) + (−2) + C = 0). In $HCOO^-$, C = +2.
(2) Correct: The change for carbon is 2 units, matched by 2 Ag(+1 to 0) or 2 Cu(+2 to +1).
(3) Incorrect: The product is $Cu_2O$, in which Cu is +1, not metallic copper.
(4) Correct: N stays at −3, and O and H in $OH^-$ are unchanged. HCHO is the reductant.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Apply the classical definitions to the reaction $2H_2S(g) + SO_2(g) \rightarrow 3S(s) + 2H_2O(l)$. Which description is correct?
options: H2S is oxidised (removal of hydrogen) and SO2 is reduced (removal of oxygen)
H2S is reduced (removal of hydrogen) and SO2 is oxidised (removal of oxygen)
Both H2S and SO2 are oxidised, since both form elemental sulphur
Both H2S and SO2 are reduced, since water is formed
questions.explanation:
H2S changes to S by losing hydrogen. Removal of hydrogen is oxidation.
SO2 changes to S by losing oxygen. Removal of oxygen is reduction.
Oxidation and reduction occur together, which fits the redox idea.
Options (3) and (4) are impossible, because a reaction cannot have only oxidation or only reduction. Option (2) swaps the definitions.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Thiosulphate reacts with iodine and with bromine as follows:
2S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ + I$_2$ → S$_4$O$_6^{2-}$ + 2I$^-$
S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ + 4Br$_2$ + 5H$_2$O → 2SO$_4^{2-}$ + 8Br$^-$ + 10H$^+$
Statement I: One S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ ion loses 8 electrons in its reaction with bromine but only 1 electron in its reaction with iodine.
Statement II: Bromine converts thiosulphate to sulphate because bromine is a weaker oxidising agent than iodine.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Average S in S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ is +2.
With I$_2$: S goes to +2.5 in S$_4$O$_6^{2-}$. That is 0.5 per S × 2 S = 1 e$^-$ per ion.
With Br$_2$: S goes to +6 in SO$_4^{2-}$. That is 4 per S × 2 S = 8 e$^-$ per ion.
So Statement I is correct.
Statement II is incorrect. Br$_2$ is the stronger oxidant ($E^\circ$ = 1.09 V versus 0.54 V for I$_2$), which is why it oxidises S further, up to +6.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In the formation of NaCl from its elements, sodium acts as the reducing agent.
(ii) Half reactions that involve gain of electrons are called oxidation reactions.
(iii) In NaH, the hydrogen atom has gained an electron.
(iv) In the formation of $Na_2S$, sulphur is oxidised because an electropositive element is added to it.
(v) Adding the two half reactions gives the overall redox reaction.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Na donates electrons, so it is the reducing agent.
(ii) Incorrect: gain of electrons is reduction.
(iii) Correct: hydrogen is present as $H^-$.
(iv) Incorrect: adding an electropositive element means reduction, so sulphur is reduced.
(v) Correct: the electrons cancel when the half reactions are summed.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In how many of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation number of –1?
$H_2O$, $NaH$, $HCl$, $CaH_2$, $NH_3$, $LiH$
questions.explanation:
By NCERT's rule, hydrogen is –1 when it is bonded to a metal in a binary compound. Otherwise it is +1.
Hydrogen is –1 in $NaH$, $CaH_2$ and $LiH$, which are metal hydrides.
Hydrogen is +1 in $H_2O$, $HCl$ and $NH_3$, where it is bonded to more electronegative non-metals.
So the count is 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion, $S_4O_6^{2-}$?
questions.explanation:
Let the oxidation number of S be x.
For the ion: $4x + 6(-2) = -2$, so $4x = 10$ and $x = +2.5$.
This is only an average. The structure shows the two end S atoms at +5 and the two middle S atoms at 0, and $\frac{5+0+0+5}{4} = 2.5$.
The value +5 is the state of the terminal sulphurs only, not the average.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
options: $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)$
$2NaH(s) \rightarrow 2Na(s) + H_2(g)$
$2KClO_3(s) \rightarrow 2KCl(s) + 3O_2(g)$
$CaCO_3(s) \rightarrow CaO(s) + CO_2(g)$
questions.explanation:
A decomposition is redox only if some oxidation numbers change.
(1) H goes from +1 to 0 and O from –2 to 0, so it is redox.
(2) Na goes from +1 to 0 and H from –1 to 0, so it is redox.
(3) Cl goes from +5 to –1 and O from –2 to 0, so it is redox.
(4) Ca stays +2, C stays +4 and O stays –2. No change occurs, so it is not redox.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Every decomposition reaction is a redox reaction.
(ii) $F_2$ cannot be obtained from $F^-$ by any chemical oxidising agent; it is obtained only by electrolytic oxidation.
(iii) With $HNO_3$, the $PbO_2$ part of $Pb_3O_4$ remains unreacted, while the $PbO$ part undergoes an acid–base reaction.
(iv) In $2Cu_2O + Cu_2S \rightarrow 6Cu + SO_2$, copper from both $Cu_2O$ and $Cu_2S$ is reduced.
(v) Silver and gold do not liberate hydrogen even from hydrochloric acid.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$ involves no change in oxidation number, so it is not redox.
(ii) Correct: fluorine is the strongest oxidant, so no chemical can oxidise $F^-$.
(iii) Correct: $HNO_3$ is itself an oxidant and does not react with $PbO_2$. Basic $PbO$ forms $Pb(NO_3)_2$.
(iv) Correct: Cu goes from +1 to 0 in both compounds, while S goes from –2 to +4.
(v) Correct: Ag and Au are very less active metals.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In acidic medium, one dichromate ion, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$, oxidises exactly six $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ions to $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$.
Reason (R): Each chromium atom in $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ goes from +6 to +3. Each dichromate ion has two Cr atoms, so it gains 6 electrons in total.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: Cr changes from +6 to +3, a gain of 3 electrons per Cr atom. Two Cr atoms give 6 electrons per dichromate ion.
A is true: each $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ loses only 1 electron, so 6 $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ are needed per dichromate ion.
The net equation is $\mathrm{6Fe^{2+} + Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ \rightarrow 6Fe^{3+} + 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O}$.
R directly explains the 1 : 6 ratio in A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Redox Reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (type of redox reaction):
List-I
A. $3Mg(s) + N_2(g) \rightarrow Mg_3N_2(s)$
B. $2KClO_3(s) \rightarrow 2KCl(s) + 3O_2(g)$
C. $V_2O_5(s) + 5Ca(s) \rightarrow 2V(s) + 5CaO(s)$
D. $2Na(s) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + H_2(g)$
List-II
(i) Metal displacement
(ii) Combination
(iii) Non-metal displacement
(iv) Decomposition
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(iii)
questions.explanation:
A: Two elements combine to give one compound, so it is a combination reaction (ii).
B: One compound breaks down and gives elemental O2, so it is a decomposition reaction (iv).
C: Ca displaces the metal V from its oxide, so it is metal displacement (i).
D: Na displaces hydrogen, a non-metal, from water, so it is non-metal displacement (iii).
Answer: (1)
